---

## 3. Model List & Root-Level Fallback Nesting

The `model_list` array defines the virtual routing topology presented to clients.

### Root-Level `fallbacks: [...]` Nesting Architecture

Each entry in `model_list` defines:
1. `model_name`: The virtual alias or model identifier requested by the client (e.g., `"fast"`, `"reasoning"`, `"gpt-4o"`).
2. `routing_strategy`: The balancing algorithm across sibling deployments (`"weighted-shuffle"`, `"least-busy"`, `"latency-based"`, `"lowest-cost"`, `"usage-based-headroom"`).
3. `fallbacks`: **Explicit root-level array** of fallback model names triggered when this model group experiences an outage, exhausted retries, or rate limit rejections.
4. `model_params`: Upstream target configuration (`model`, `api_key`, `weight`, `rpm`, `tpm`, `azure_deployment_name`, etc.).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Client["Client Request: model: 'gpt-4o'"] --> Primary["Primary Group: gpt-4o<br/>(openai/gpt-4o)"]
    Primary -->|"HTTP 429 / 5xx & Retries Exhausted"| FB1["Fallback 1: claude-3-5-sonnet<br/>(anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet)"]
    FB1 -->|"HTTP 429 / 5xx & Retries Exhausted"| FB2["Fallback 2: gemini-2.5-pro<br/>(gemini/gemini-2.5-pro)"]
    FB2 -->|Success| Response["200 OK (X-Gateway-Provider: gemini)"]
```

### Declarative Example: Multi-Tier Failover

```yaml
model_list:
  # Primary Tier: GPT-4o with cross-cloud fallbacks
  - model_name: "gpt-4o"
    routing_strategy: "weighted-shuffle"
    fallbacks:
      - "claude-3-5-sonnet"
      - "gemini-2.5-pro"
    model_params:
      model: "openai/gpt-4o"
      api_key: "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY"
      weight: 100
      rpm: 1000
      tpm: 80000

  # Fallback Tier 1: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
  - model_name: "claude-3-5-sonnet"
    routing_strategy: "latency-based"
    fallbacks:
      - "gemini-2.5-pro"
    model_params:
      model: "anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022"
      api_key: "os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
      weight: 100

  # Fallback Tier 2: Gemini 2.5 Pro
  - model_name: "gemini-2.5-pro"
    routing_strategy: "weighted-shuffle"
    model_params:
      model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-pro"
      api_key: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY"
      weight: 100

  # High-Throughput "fast" Group: Multi-Provider Load Balancing
  - model_name: "fast"
    routing_strategy: "least-busy"
    fallbacks:
      - "fast-backup"
    model_params:
      model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"
      api_key: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY"
      weight: 70

  - model_name: "fast"
    routing_strategy: "least-busy"
    model_params:
      model: "openai/gpt-4o-mini"
      api_key: "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY"
      weight: 30

  # Emergency Local Backup
  - model_name: "fast-backup"
    routing_strategy: "weighted-shuffle"
    model_params:
      model: "ollama/llama3.3"
      api_base: "http://localhost:11434"
      weight: 100
```

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `fallbacks: [...]` slice is declared at the root level of each `model_list` entry alongside `model_name` and `model_params`. It must never be nested inside the `model_params` object. The router traverses fallbacks strictly in listed order, respecting circuit breaker states for each candidate before dispatching.

---

## Deployment and Storage Architecture
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/operations/deployment-and-storage
Section: Guides & Platform Documentation > Deployment & Platform Ops

# Deployment and Storage Architecture

GoRoute AI Gateway supports two operational storage modes:
1. **In-Memory Mode (`storage.mode: memory`)**: Zero external dependencies. Ideal for local unit testing, CI pipelines, and ephemeral container runs. Secrets are kept in-process in an AES-256-GCM vault, but state does not survive process restarts.
2. **Clustered PostgreSQL + Redis (`storage.mode: postgres`)**: The enterprise production topology. PostgreSQL provides ACID durability for multi-tenant organizations, model catalogs, encrypted credentials, virtual keys, audit trails, stateful files, and asynchronous batch jobs. Redis (`go-redis` `UniversalClient`) supports standalone, Sentinel (`storage.redis_master_name`), and Cluster (`storage.redis_addrs`) modes for distributed L2 key caching, atomic sliding-window rate limiting, response caching, circuit breaker state, and real-time Pub/Sub streams.

For production Kubernetes deployments using the hardened manifests in `deployments/k8s/`, see the [Kubernetes Kustomize Deployment Guide](/docs/operations/kubernetes-kustomize).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Clients["Inference & Management Clients"]
        HTTPClients["OpenAI / Anthropic SDKs"]
        OperatorUI["Operator Web UI (/ui/)"]
        AgentClients["MCP / A2A Clients"]
    end

    subgraph Cluster["Gateway Cluster Pods"]
        Pod1["GoRoute Pod 1"]
        Pod2["GoRoute Pod 2"]
    end

    subgraph Storage["Clustered Persistence Layer"]
        PG[("PostgreSQL 16+<br/>(16 Persistent Tables & Migrations)")]
        Redis[("Redis 7+<br/>(L2 Caching, Rate Limiting, Pub/Sub)")]
    end

    Clients --> Pod1
    Clients --> Pod2
    Pod1 --> PG
    Pod2 --> PG
    Pod1 <--> Redis
    Pod2 <--> Redis
```

---

## 1. PostgreSQL Schema Migrations (0001 to 0012)

The gateway automatically manages its database schema at startup using embedded SQL migration scripts located in `migrations/`. Migrations are applied sequentially inside an atomic transaction (note that `0009` does not exist; numbering advances from `0008` directly to `0010`).

| Migration File | Description | Core Operations |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`0001_init_schema.up.sql`** | Core Schema Initialization | Enables `pgcrypto`. Creates base multi-tenant tables (`global_models`, `organizations`, `org_provider_subscriptions`, `org_model_policies`, `teams`, `users`, `virtual_keys`, `provider_credentials`, `model_groups`, `model_deployments`, `spend_logs`, `audit_logs`). |
| **`0002_add_platform_modules.up.sql`** | Platform Governance & Guardrails | Introduces `model_pricing_history` (immutable audit log of token pricing changes) and `guardrail_policies` (PII masking and prompt injection rules). |
| **`0003_add_mcp_and_a2a.up.sql`** | MCP Hub & A2A Network Tables | Creates MCP entity tables (`mcp_servers`, `mcp_tools`, `mcp_toolsets`, `mcp_user_credentials`) and A2A tables (`a2a_agents`, `a2a_tasks`, `a2a_task_events`, `a2a_stream_publications`, `a2a_outbox_events`, `a2a_push_notification_configs`). |
| **`0004_add_pricing_status.up.sql`** | Pricing Provenance & Azure Fields | Adds `pricing_status`, `pricing_provenance_source`, and `pricing_effective_date` to `global_models` and `spend_logs`. Adds `azure_deployment_name` and `api_version` to `provider_credentials`. Backfills audited seed models. |
| **`0005_add_model_capabilities.up.sql`** | Persistent Capabilities & Provenance | Adds `capabilities` JSONB column to `global_models` for tri-state capabilities tracking. Adds `pricing_status` and `pricing_provenance_source` to `model_pricing_history`. |
| **`0006_add_supports_inference.up.sql`** | Non-Inference Product Segregation | Adds `supports_inference` boolean flag to `global_models` to distinguish callable LLM deployments from ancillary catalog products. |
| **`0007_add_modality_pricing_and_spend.up.sql`** | Multi-Modal Spend & Batch Assets | Adds modality pricing columns (`rerank_cost_micros_per_search_unit`, `image_cost_micros_base`, `audio_stt_cost_micros_per_second`, etc.) to `global_models`, adds `modality` and `modality_units` JSONB to `spend_logs`, and creates `files` (`file_uploads`) and `batches` tables. |
| **`0008_add_spend_event_outbox.up.sql`** | Durable Spend Event Outbox | Creates `spend_event_outbox` (`pending`, `processing`, `delivered`, `dead_letter`) with retry/lock indexes for durable, idempotent Redis/PostgreSQL spend reconciliation. |
| **`0010_guardrail_mode.up.sql`** | `logging_only` Guardrails & All-Role Scanning | Adds `mode` (`enforce` / `logging_only`) and `scan_all_roles` columns to `guardrail_policies`. *(Note: `0009` does not exist.)* |
| **`0011_budget_reset_outbox.up.sql`** | Budget Reset Outbox | Creates `budget_reset_outbox` (`org`, `team`, `key` scopes) so expired budget period rollovers in PostgreSQL reliably clear Redis spend counters. |
| **`0012_add_cache_write_and_operations.up.sql`** | Cache-Write Pricing & Operations | Adds `cache_write_cost_micros_per_1m` and `supported_operations` JSONB to `global_models` for prompt cache-write FinOps and `SupportedOperations` routing enforcement. *(v1.6.0 also removes invalid `::uuid` casts on `VARCHAR(64)` `org_id`/`team_id`/`user_id` columns in `file_uploads` queries.)* |

---

## 2. The 16 Persistent Table Schemas

### 1. `global_models`
Stores the unified catalog of all discovered and manually registered LLMs across providers.
```sql
CREATE TABLE global_models (
    id                              VARCHAR(128) PRIMARY KEY, -- e.g. "openai/gpt-4o", "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"
    provider                        VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
    model_name                      VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    display_name                    VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    max_input_tokens                INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 128000,
    max_output_tokens               INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 16384,
    supports_streaming              BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    supports_tools                  BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    supports_vision                 BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    supports_reasoning              BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    supports_embeddings             BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    supports_inference              BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    capabilities                    JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    input_cost_micros_per_1m        BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    output_cost_micros_per_1m       BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cached_input_cost_micros_per_1m BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    reasoning_cost_micros_per_1m    BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    rerank_cost_micros_per_search_unit BIGINT    DEFAULT 0,
    image_cost_micros_base          BIGINT       DEFAULT 0,
    image_cost_micros_hd            BIGINT       DEFAULT 0,
    audio_stt_cost_micros_per_second BIGINT      DEFAULT 0,
    audio_tts_cost_micros_per_1k_chars BIGINT    DEFAULT 0,
    modality_pricing_json           JSONB        DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    pricing_status                  VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown',
    pricing_provenance_source       VARCHAR(255),
    pricing_effective_date          VARCHAR(64),
    lifecycle_status                VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    deprecation_date                TIMESTAMPTZ,
    metadata                        JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    discovered_at                   TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at                      TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (provider, model_name)
);
```

### 2. `organizations`
Multi-tenant root container managing corporate spend caps, RPM/TPM ceilings, and billing cycles.
```sql
CREATE TABLE organizations (
    id                  VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    name                VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    slug                VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    max_budget_micros   BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- 0 = unlimited
    spent_micros        BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    budget_reset_period VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monthly', -- 'daily', 'monthly', 'never'
    budget_reset_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    rpm_limit           INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tpm_limit           INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    is_active           BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    metadata            JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 3. `org_provider_subscriptions`
Layer 2 governance controlling which upstream cloud providers an organization is permitted to call.
```sql
CREATE TABLE org_provider_subscriptions (
    org_id          VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    provider        VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
    is_enabled      BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    auto_enable_new BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    subscribed_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    PRIMARY KEY (org_id, provider)
);
```

### 4. `org_model_policies`
Layer 3 governance allowing or forbidding specific catalog models within an organization.
```sql
CREATE TABLE org_model_policies (
    org_id          VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    global_model_id VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL REFERENCES global_models(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    is_enabled      BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    approved_by     VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'system',
    approved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    PRIMARY KEY (org_id, global_model_id)
);
```

### 5. `teams`
Sub-organizational entities representing engineering squads, divisions, or departments.
```sql
CREATE TABLE teams (
    id                  VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id              VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name                VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    max_budget_micros   BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    spent_micros        BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    budget_reset_period VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monthly',
    budget_reset_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    rpm_limit           INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tpm_limit           INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    allowed_models      TEXT[]       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    is_active           BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at          TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (org_id, name)
);
```

### 6. `users`
Individual human operators or service accounts bound to organizations and teams.
```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id         VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id     VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    team_id    VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES teams(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    email      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    role       VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member', -- 'admin', 'member', 'read_only'
    is_active  BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (org_id, email)
);
```

### 7. `virtual_keys`
Client authentication bearer tokens with rate limits, budgets, and model allowlists.
```sql
CREATE TABLE virtual_keys (
    id                VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id            VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    team_id           VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES teams(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    user_id           VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    name              VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    key_hash          VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL UNIQUE, -- SHA-256 hash of secret part
    key_prefix        VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,        -- Display prefix e.g. "sk-gw-a1b2"
    allowed_models    TEXT[]       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{"*"}',
    allowed_endpoints TEXT[]       NOT NULL DEFAULT '{"*"}',
    max_budget_micros BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    spent_micros      BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    rpm_limit         INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tpm_limit         INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    expires_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
    is_active         BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    metadata          JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 8. `provider_credentials`
AES-256-GCM encrypted storage for upstream provider API keys and cloud service account credentials.
```sql
CREATE TABLE provider_credentials (
    id                     VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id                 VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    provider               VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
    name                   VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    encrypted_api_key      TEXT         NOT NULL,
    key_nonce              VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    key_hash               VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    aws_access_key_id      VARCHAR(128),
    encrypted_aws_secret   TEXT,
    aws_region             VARCHAR(32),
    encrypted_gcp_sa_json  TEXT,
    gcp_project_id         VARCHAR(128),
    gcp_region             VARCHAR(32),
    azure_deployment_name  VARCHAR(255),
    api_version            VARCHAR(64),
    custom_endpoint_url    TEXT,
    is_active              BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    expires_at             TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at             TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at             TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (org_id, provider, name)
);
```

### 9. `model_groups`
Logical routing targets aggregating sibling deployments under a shared virtual alias (`"fast"`, `"reasoning"`).
```sql
CREATE TABLE model_groups (
    id               VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id           VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name             VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    routing_strategy VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'weighted_shuffle',
    fallback_group_id VARCHAR(64) REFERENCES model_groups(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at       TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE (org_id, name)
);
```

### 10. `model_deployments`
Individual physical provider routing targets bound to credentials with health and circuit breaker tracking.
```sql
CREATE TABLE model_deployments (
    id                   VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    model_group_id       VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES model_groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    global_model_id      VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL REFERENCES global_models(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    credential_id        VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES provider_credentials(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    deployment_name      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    weight               INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,
    priority             INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    rpm_limit            INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    tpm_limit            INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuit_breaker_mode VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard',
    status               VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active', -- 'active', 'degraded', 'cooldown', 'disabled'
    consecutive_failures INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cooldown_until       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    last_failure_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    last_success_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at           TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at           TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 11. `spend_logs`
High-throughput FinOps ledger recording every billable inference operation in integer micro-dollars.
```sql
CREATE TABLE spend_logs (
    id                        VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id                    VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    team_id                   VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES teams(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    user_id                   VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    virtual_key_id            VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES virtual_keys(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    deployment_id             VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES model_deployments(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    global_model_id           VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    provider                  VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
    modality                  VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'chat',
    prompt_tokens             INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    completion_tokens         INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cached_prompt_tokens      INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    reasoning_tokens          INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total_tokens              INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    modality_units            JSONB        DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    cost_micros               BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    request_duration_ms       INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    status_code               INTEGER      NOT NULL DEFAULT 200,
    error_code                VARCHAR(64),
    pricing_status            VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unrecorded',
    pricing_provenance_source VARCHAR(255),
    created_at                TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 12. `audit_logs`
Tamper-resistant audit log capturing administrative actions, policy mutations, and credential access.
```sql
CREATE TABLE audit_logs (
    id          VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id      VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id     VARCHAR(64),
    actor       VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    action      VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    resource    VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    resource_id VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    changes     JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    ip_address  VARCHAR(64),
    user_agent  TEXT,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 13. `model_pricing_history`
Immutable historical log of every catalog token and modality pricing update.
```sql
CREATE TABLE model_pricing_history (
    id                              VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    global_model_id                 VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL REFERENCES global_models(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    input_cost_micros_per_1m        BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    output_cost_micros_per_1m       BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    cached_input_cost_micros_per_1m BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    reasoning_cost_micros_per_1m    BIGINT       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    pricing_status                  VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown',
    pricing_provenance_source       VARCHAR(255),
    effective_from                  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    created_at                      TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 14. `guardrail_policies`
Content safety rules, PII detectors, and prompt injection filters attached to tenants.
```sql
CREATE TABLE guardrail_policies (
    id          VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()::text,
    org_id      VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name        VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    is_active   BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    rules       JSONB        NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
    action      VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'block', -- 'block', 'mask', 'warn'
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
```

### 15. `files`
Metadata and disk pointers for stateful tenant assets (fine-tuning datasets, Whisper audio, batch inputs).
```sql
CREATE TABLE files (
    id                VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY,
    org_id            VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    team_id           VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES teams(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    user_id           VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    bytes             BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    filename          VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    purpose           VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    status            VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'uploaded',
    content_sha256    VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    storage_path      TEXT         NOT NULL,
    upstream_provider VARCHAR(64),
    upstream_id       VARCHAR(128),
    expires_at        TIMESTAMPTZ
);
```

### 16. `batches`
Asynchronous inference batch requests evaluated within 24-hour turnaround windows for 50% discount.
```sql
CREATE TABLE batches (
    id                VARCHAR(64)  PRIMARY KEY,
    org_id            VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    team_id           VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES teams(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    input_file_id     VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL REFERENCES files(id),
    output_file_id    VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES files(id),
    error_file_id     VARCHAR(64)  REFERENCES files(id),
    endpoint          VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    status            VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL DEFAULT 'validating',
    completion_window VARCHAR(32)  NOT NULL,
    created_at        TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    completed_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
    metadata          JSONB        DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
    request_counts    JSONB        DEFAULT '{"total":0,"completed":0,"failed":0}'::jsonb,
    upstream_provider VARCHAR(64),
    upstream_id       VARCHAR(128)
);
```

## 3. Redis Cluster, Sentinel & Keyspace Matrix

`RedisFabric` (`internal/storage/redis.go`) wraps a `go-redis` `UniversalClient` protected by a circuit breaker (with `redis.Nil` cache misses treated as non-failures). It supports three deployment topologies:
- **Standalone**: `storage.redis_addr` (`GATEWAY_REDIS_ADDR`)
- **Redis Cluster**: `storage.redis_addrs` (`GATEWAY_REDIS_ADDRS`, comma-separated seed nodes)
- **Redis Sentinel**: `storage.redis_addrs` combined with `storage.redis_master_name` (`GATEWAY_REDIS_MASTER_NAME`)

All multi-key Lua scripts for rate limiting, budget reservations, and spend reconciliation use `{org:<orgID>}` hash tags (e.g., `gw:spend:{org:<orgID>}:key:{keyID}`, `gw:budget:{org:<orgID>}:reservations:key:{keyID}`) so every key belonging to an organization maps to the same Redis Cluster hash slot.

All keys are namespaced with the `gw:` prefix.

| Redis Key Pattern | Type | Configured TTL | Subsystem & Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `gw:auth:key:{keyHash}` | String | `auth.l2_cache_ttl` *(default `5m`)* | **Auth L2 Cache**: Serialized `IdentityContext` preventing database lookups on every request. |
| `gw:rl:rpm:key:{keyID}:{minute}` | String (Int) | `window_seconds * 2` *(120s)* | **Rate Limiter**: Sliding-minute requests counter for virtual key. |
| `gw:rl:tpm:key:{keyID}:{minute}` | String (Int) | `window_seconds * 2` *(120s)* | **Rate Limiter**: Sliding-minute tokens counter for virtual key. |
| `gw:rl:conc:{keyID}` | String (Int) | `rate_limit.concurrency_ttl_sec` *(300s)* | **Rate Limiter**: Atomic lease counter tracking concurrent in-flight requests. |
| `gw:spend:key:{keyID}` | String (Int) | None *(Persistent Counter)* | **FinOps**: Fast in-memory spend accumulator for virtual key. |
| `gw:rl:rpm:team:{teamID}:{minute}` | String (Int) | `window_seconds * 2` *(120s)* | **Rate Limiter**: Team-level sliding-minute requests counter. |
| `gw:rl:tpm:team:{teamID}:{minute}` | String (Int) | `window_seconds * 2` *(120s)* | **Rate Limiter**: Team-level sliding-minute tokens counter. |
| `gw:spend:team:{teamID}` | String (Int) | None *(Persistent Counter)* | **FinOps**: Team-level spend accumulator. |
| `gw:rl:rpm:org:{orgID}:{minute}` | String (Int) | `window_seconds * 2` *(120s)* | **Rate Limiter**: Organization-level sliding-minute requests counter. |
| `gw:rl:tpm:org:{orgID}:{minute}` | String (Int) | `window_seconds * 2` *(120s)* | **Rate Limiter**: Organization-level sliding-minute tokens counter. |
| `gw:spend:org:{orgID}` | String (Int) | None *(Persistent Counter)* | **FinOps**: Organization-level spend accumulator. |
| `gw:cache:resp:{sha256(req)}` | String (JSON) | Configured Cache TTL *(default `1h`)* | **Response Cache**: Exact-match cached `CanonicalChatResponse`. |
| `gw:router:cooldown:{depID}` | String | `router.default_cooldown` *(default `60s`)* | **Circuit Breaker**: Cooldown lock asserting deployment is in `OPEN` state. |
| `gw:lock:discovery` | String | `60s` | **Discovery Worker**: Distributed leader election lock preventing duplicate sync sweeps. |
| `gw:mcp:hdl:{handle}` | String (JSON) | `mcp.handle_ttl` *(default `1h`)* | **MCP Discovery**: 256-bit opaque tool handle record binding. |
| `gw:events:invalidation` | Pub/Sub Channel | N/A | **Cluster Invalidation**: Broadcasts L1 cache eviction events when keys or policies mutate. |
| `gw:a2a:events:{taskID}` | Pub/Sub Channel | N/A | **A2A Streaming**: Real-time event bus broadcasting SSE updates to connected subscribers. |

> [!TIP]
> In production environments with multiple gateway pods, always configure Redis so that virtual key revocations and policy modifications broadcast via `gw:events:invalidation` take effect across all pods within milliseconds.

---

## Kubernetes & Kustomize Deployment
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/operations/kubernetes-kustomize
Section: Guides & Platform Documentation > Deployment & Platform Ops

# Kubernetes & Kustomize Deployment

GoRoute AI Gateway ships production-hardened Kubernetes manifests under [`deployments/k8s/`](https://github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/tree/main/deployments/k8s) managed via Kustomize. The base overlay deploys a 2-replica stateless gateway tier backed by PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7, with non-root container hardening, read-only root filesystems, and `/readyz` + `/healthz` probes.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Ingress["Ingress / Load Balancer"] --> Svc["Service: gateway (ClusterIP :8080)"]
    Svc --> Pod1["Pod: gateway-1<br/>non-root UID 65532, readOnlyRootFS"]
    Svc --> Pod2["Pod: gateway-2<br/>non-root UID 65532, readOnlyRootFS"]
    Pod1 --> PGSvc["Service: postgres (:5432)<br/>PostgreSQL 16"]
    Pod2 --> PGSvc
    Pod1 <--> RedisSvc["Service: redis (:6379)<br/>Redis 7 / Cluster / Sentinel"]
    Pod2 <--> RedisSvc
    Prom["Prometheus Scraper"] -->|Bearer Admin Key<br/>GET /metrics| Svc
```

---

## 1. Kustomize Manifest Inventory

The `deployments/k8s/kustomization.yaml` file composes six resource manifests into a single deployable unit:

| File | Kind | Name | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `namespace.yaml` | `Namespace` | `goroute-test` | Isolates gateway, database, and cache resources (override in production overlays). |
| `postgres.yaml` | `Deployment`, `Service` | `postgres` | PostgreSQL 16 (`postgres:16-alpine`) on port `5432` with `pg_isready` readiness probe. |
| `redis.yaml` | `Deployment`, `Service` | `redis` | Redis 7 (`redis:7-alpine`) on port `6379` with `redis-cli ping` readiness probe. |
| `secret.example.yaml` | `Secret` | `gateway-secrets` | Template secret injecting `GATEWAY_POSTGRES_DSN`, `GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY`, and `GATEWAY_MASTER_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. |
| `gateway-deployment.yaml` | `Deployment` | `gateway` | 2-replica GoRoute AI Gateway (`goroute/ai-gateway`) with hardened security context and probes. |
| `service.yaml` | `Service` | `gateway` | Exposes port `8080` (`http`) across the `app: gateway` replica set. |

---

## 2. Applying the Manifests

Preview the rendered manifests before applying:

```bash
kubectl kustomize deployments/k8s/
```

Deploy to your cluster:

```bash
kubectl apply -k deployments/k8s/
kubectl -n goroute-test rollout status deployment/gateway --timeout=120s
```

To verify the multi-replica Kubernetes smoke suite locally against a `kind` or `k3d` cluster, run:

```bash
make test-k8s-smoke
```

:::warning Replace Example Secrets Before Production
`deployments/k8s/secret.example.yaml` contains placeholder test credentials. Never apply example secrets to a production cluster. Use External Secrets Operator, Sealed Secrets, or a Kustomize `secretGenerator` overlay backed by your KMS/Vault.
:::

---

## 3. Container Security Context & Probes

`deployments/k8s/gateway-deployment.yaml` enforces strict pod and container hardening:

- **Pod `securityContext`**: `runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 65532` (distroless non-root user).
- **Container `securityContext`**:
  - `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`
  - `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`
  - `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`
- **Graceful Shutdown**: `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30` paired with `server.shutdown_timeout` (`15s` default) to drain active SSE streams.
- **Resource Requests & Limits**: Requests `100m` CPU / `128Mi` memory; limits `500m` CPU / `512Mi` memory (tune upward for high-concurrency streaming or large multipart file uploads).
- **Health Probes**:
  - **Readiness (`GET /readyz` on `:8080`)**: `initialDelaySeconds: 3`, `periodSeconds: 5`. Verifies live PostgreSQL and Redis connectivity before routing traffic.
  - **Liveness (`GET /healthz` on `:8080`)**: `initialDelaySeconds: 5`, `periodSeconds: 10`. Confirms process health without cascading restarts on transient dependency blips.

:::tip Writable Scratch Volume for Multipart File Uploads
If you enable `/v1/files` or audio multipart disk spooling (`POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`) with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, mount an `emptyDir` volume at `/tmp` (or your configured temp/file storage path) so Go's multipart spooled files can write safely.
:::

---

## 4. Production Overlay: Namespace, Secrets & Image Tag

Create a production Kustomize overlay (e.g., `deployments/k8s/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml`) rather than editing the base manifests directly:

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: goroute-prod

resources:
  - ../../

images:
  - name: goroute/ai-gateway
    newTag: v1.6.0

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Namespace
      name: goroute-test
    patch: |-
      - op: replace
        path: /metadata/name
        value: goroute-prod
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: gateway
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-
        value:
          name: GATEWAY_ENV
          value: "production"
```

---

## 5. PostgreSQL 16 & Redis Cluster / Sentinel

### PostgreSQL 16
The base `postgres.yaml` uses `postgres:16-alpine` with a single replica for smoke testing. For production:
- Use a managed PostgreSQL 16+ service (RDS, Cloud SQL, Neon) or a HA operator (CloudNativePG) with TLS (`?sslmode=verify-full`) in `GATEWAY_POSTGRES_DSN`.
- Embedded SQL migrations (`0001` through `0012`) run automatically at startup inside atomic transactions.

### Redis Cluster & Sentinel
GoRoute's `RedisFabric` uses `go-redis` `UniversalClient` with `{org:<id>}` hash-tagged keys so multi-key Lua scripts for rate limiting and response caching execute atomically on a single slot:

| Topology | Environment Variables |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Standalone** | `GATEWAY_REDIS_ADDR=redis:6379` |
| **Redis Cluster** | `GATEWAY_REDIS_ADDRS=redis-0:6379,redis-1:6379,redis-2:6379` |
| **Redis Sentinel** | `GATEWAY_REDIS_ADDRS=sentinel-0:26379,sentinel-1:26379,sentinel-2:26379` + `GATEWAY_REDIS_MASTER_NAME=mymaster` |
| **Authentication** | `GATEWAY_REDIS_PASS=<password>` |

---

## 6. Prometheus Metrics Scraping

The `GET /metrics` endpoint exposes Prometheus text format `0.0.4` metrics using bounded-cardinality reservoir sampling (`1,024` samples) and requires `Authorization: Bearer <GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY>`.

Configure a Prometheus `ServiceMonitor` or `ScrapeConfig` referencing the admin bearer token secret:

```yaml
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: goroute-gateway
  namespace: goroute-prod
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  endpoints:
    - port: http
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s
      bearerTokenSecret:
        name: gateway-secrets
        key: GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY
```

See [Observability, Metrics & Health Probes](./observability.md) for the full exported metric catalog and OTLP tracing configuration.

## Go SDK Overview
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/sdk/overview
Section: Go SDK Handbook > Go SDK Handbook

# Go SDK Overview

Package: `github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway`. The SDK provides a Go client for chat requests and common gateway operations. It can start a gateway instance in the current process or connect to an HTTP gateway service.

## Choose a mode

| Mode | Constructor | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Embedded | `gateway.New(...)` | Loads gateway configuration, starts an in-process gateway server, and returns a client that talks to it over HTTP. |
| Remote | `gateway.NewClient(url, key)` or `gateway.WithRemote(url, key)` | Sends requests to an already running gateway service. |

The embedded mode does not require a separately deployed gateway service. It still runs the gateway server and uses HTTP internally; it is not a direct function call into the inference handler.

## Requirements and installation

The upstream module currently declares Go `1.26.0` in `go.mod`. Use a compatible Go toolchain:

```bash
go get github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway@v1.5.0
```

## Minimal request

```go
ctx := context.Background()
gw, err := gateway.New(
	gateway.WithModelList(gateway.ModelEntry{
		ModelName: "fast",
		Model:     "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash",
		APIKey:    "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY",
	}),
	gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
defer gw.Close()

result, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Explain what an AI gateway does.")
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(result.Content)
```

This is a function-body example; it assumes `context`, `fmt`, and the gateway package are imported and is inside a function that can return an error. The mock option provides a local fallback when the referenced environment key is unset. To verify a real provider call, configure a valid key and omit the mock option.

- [Chat and streaming](./chat-and-streaming)

- [MCP and A2A](./mcp-and-a2a)
- [Public SDK types and methods](./go-sdk-reference)

## Client Initialization & Configuration
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/sdk/client-configuration
Section: Go SDK Handbook > Go SDK Handbook

# Client Initialization & Configuration

The `pkg/gateway` package uses functional options to configure an embedded gateway or a remote gateway client.

---

## 1. Initializing the Client

### `gateway.New(opts ...Option) (*Client, error)`

Initializes a client. If `WithRemote(...)` is provided, it connects to that remote service. Otherwise, it loads configuration and starts an embedded gateway server in the current process:

```go
gw, err := gateway.New(
    gateway.WithModelList(
        gateway.ModelEntry{ModelName: "fast", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"},
    ),
    gateway.WithLogLevel("info"),
)
if err != nil {
    log.Fatalf("failed to initialize: %v", err)
}
defer gw.Close()
```

### `gateway.NewClient(baseURL, apiKey string) *Client`

Creates an HTTP client pointing to an already-running GoRoute server or container:

```go
client := gateway.NewClient("http://localhost:8080", "sk-gw-developer-key")
```

---

## 2. Configuration Options

### `WithModelList(entries ...ModelEntry) Option`

Configures the embedded router with declarative model aliases, fallbacks, and routing strategies.

```go
gw, err := gateway.New(
    gateway.WithModelList(
        gateway.ModelEntry{
            ModelName:       "smart-router",
            Model:           "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash",
            APIKey:          "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY",
            RoutingStrategy: "least-busy",
            Fallbacks:       []string{"backup-claude"},
            RPM:             1000,
            TPM:             500000,
        },
        gateway.ModelEntry{
            ModelName: "backup-claude",
            Model:     "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
            APIKey:    "os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
        },
    ),
)
```

#### `ModelEntry` Specification

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ModelName` | `string` | Client-facing alias (e.g. `"fast"`, `"reasoning"`, `"auto"`). |
| `Model` | `string` | Upstream provider/model identifier (e.g. `"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"`, `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`, `"openai/gpt-4.1-mini"`). |
| `APIKey` | `string` | Upstream API key string or environment reference (e.g. `"os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY"`). |
| `APIBase` | `string` | Optional custom endpoint URL (e.g. for Ollama or private vLLM clusters: `"http://localhost:11434"`). |
| `RoutingStrategy`| `string` | Routing policy: `"weighted-shuffle"`, `"least-busy"`, `"latency-based"`, `"usage-based-headroom"`, or `"lowest-cost"`. |
| `Fallbacks` | `[]string`| Ordered list of model aliases to invoke if this model returns 429, 503, or times out. |
| `Weight` | `int` | Integer weight for `"weighted-shuffle"` distribution. |
| `RPM` | `int` | Requests Per Minute limit enforced across this model entry. |
| `TPM` | `int` | Tokens Per Minute limit enforced across this model entry. |
| `SimulateStatus` | `int` | Optional fault injection HTTP code (e.g. `503`) to test circuit breakers and fallback chains offline. |

---

### `WithConfigFile(path string) Option`

Loads model definitions, rate limits, and security policies from an external YAML file:

```go
gw, err := gateway.New(
    gateway.WithConfigFile("./config/gateway.yaml"),
)
```

**Sample YAML (`gateway.yaml`):**
```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: "production-fast"
    model_params:
      model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"
      api_key: "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY"
      rpm: 1000
    fallbacks: ["production-backup"]
  - model_name: "production-backup"
    model_params:
      model: "openai/gpt-4.1-mini"
      api_key: "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

---

### `WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing() Option`

Enables built-in local mock HTTP servers for any `ModelEntry` whose environment variable API key is not present. This allows unit tests, integration tests, and local demos to run immediately without requiring live provider credentials or incurring costs.

```go
gw, err := gateway.New(
    gateway.WithModelList(
        gateway.ModelEntry{ModelName: "test-model", Model: "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"},
    ),
    gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(), // Mock provider handles requests locally
)
```

---

### Logging Options

Control internal gateway logging using Go standard library's `log/slog`:

- **`WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option`**: Provide a custom `slog.Logger` instance.
- **`WithSilentLogs() Option`**: Suppress all stdout/stderr logs (ideal for CLI tools or clean terminal outputs).
- **`WithLogLevel(level string) Option`**: Set minimum log level (`"debug"`, `"info"`, `"warn"`, `"error"`).

```go
customLogger := slog.New(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stdout, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: slog.LevelDebug}))

gw, err := gateway.New(
    gateway.WithLogger(customLogger),
)
```

---

### `WithRemote(baseURL, apiKey string) Option`

Redirects `gateway.New` to connect to a remote gateway daemon instead of starting an embedded router:

```go
gw, err := gateway.New(
    gateway.WithRemote("https://ai-gateway.company.com", "sk-gw-production"),
)
```

---

## 3. Client Lifecycle & Scoping

### Dynamic Key Switching with `WithKey`

In multi-tenant backend services, create a shallow copy of the client with a tenant's specific Virtual API Key. The base connection and connection pooling are shared:

```go
// Base client initialized once at service startup
masterClient, _ := gateway.New(...)

// HTTP handler for tenant A
func TenantAHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    tenantKey := r.Header.Get("X-Tenant-Key")
    tenantClient := masterClient.WithKey(tenantKey)

    // Chat requests are now governed by tenantKey's budget, rate limits, and model allowances
    res, err := tenantClient.Chat(r.Context(), "fast", "Process tenant query")
    ...
}
```

### Teardown with `Close`

For embedded instances, `Close()` cleanly shuts down background workers, flushes remaining telemetry events, and terminates local mock servers:

```go
defer gw.Close()
```

*(For remote clients created via `NewClient`, `Close()` is a safe no-op).*

### Endpoint Inspection with `BaseURL`

Inspect the loopback HTTP URL generated for the in-process server (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:54321`):

```go
fmt.Printf("Embedded gateway listening internally on: %s\n", gw.BaseURL())
```

---

## Chat and Streaming
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/sdk/chat-and-streaming
Section: Go SDK Handbook > Go SDK Handbook

# Chat and Streaming

The SDK exposes `Chat` for a single user prompt, `ChatWithMessages` for structured history, and `StreamChat` for receiving text deltas through a callback. The examples below are function-body snippets and assume `ctx context.Context`, an initialized `gw`, and the standard imports.

## Single-prompt chat

```go
result, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Draft a short status update.",
	gateway.WithSystem("You are a concise engineering assistant."),
	gateway.WithTemperature(0.4),
	gateway.WithMaxTokens(256),
)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(result.Content)
```

Available request options are `WithSystem`, `WithTemperature`, `WithMaxTokens`, and `WithReasoningEffort`. The upstream provider determines which options it supports.

## Multi-turn chat

```go
result, err := gw.ChatWithMessages(ctx, gateway.ChatRequest{
	Model: "fast",
	Messages: []gateway.Message{
		{Role: "system", Content: "You are a concise site reliability engineer."},
		{Role: "user", Content: "What should I check first after an HTTP 504?"},
		{Role: "assistant", Content: "Check the gateway, upstream health, and timeout logs."},
		{Role: "user", Content: "How can I narrow it down?"},
	},
})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(result.Content)
```

## Stream text deltas

`StreamChat` calls `onDelta` as text arrives from the upstream stream. The callback can return an error to stop processing.

```go
result, err := gw.StreamChat(ctx, "fast", "Write a short haiku about Go.", func(delta string) error {
	_, err := fmt.Print(delta)
	return err
})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Printf("\nCost: %d µ$\n", result.CostMicros)
```

The gateway translates supported provider streaming responses into the SDK callback. Delivery timing and available content depend on the selected provider; no fixed latency or buffering guarantee is implied.

## Set a deadline

Pass a context with a timeout to bound the request and cancel work when the caller no longer needs the response:

```go
requestCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()

result, err := gw.Chat(requestCtx, "fast", "Summarize this report.")
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println(result.Content)
```

## Inspect result fields

`ChatResult` provides top-level fields for content, provider, model, request ID, cost in micro-dollars, routing time in microseconds, cache status, and whether a fallback was attempted. `Usage` and `Raw` expose internal domain types; prefer the top-level fields when you need a stable public SDK surface.

For function/tool definitions and the HTTP request shape, see [Tool Calling](/docs/data-plane/tool-calling). The current public SDK request type does not expose a `tools` field.

---

## Virtual Keys and FinOps
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/sdk/virtual-keys-and-finops
Section: Go SDK Handbook > Go SDK Handbook

# Virtual Keys and FinOps

The SDK provides methods for creating and revoking virtual keys and reading the spend summary. These are administrative operations: use a client configured with the gateway admin credential and protect it as a privileged object.

## Create a virtual key

```go
key, err := adminClient.CreateVirtualKey(ctx, gateway.VirtualKeyRequest{
	Name:            "payments-service",
	OrgID:           "org_default",
	Role:            "service_account",
	MaxBudgetMicros: 25_000_000, // 25 USD
	RPMLimit:        120,
	TPMLimit:        100_000,
	AllowedModels:   []string{"fast"},
})
if err != nil {
	return err
}

// Store key.Key in an approved secret store; do not log or commit it.
fmt.Println("Created key ID:", key.ID)
```

`MaxBudgetMicros` uses micro-dollars (`1 USD = 1,000,000 µ$`). The returned `key.Key` contains the new secret and is only available in the creation response. Store it securely.

## Use a scoped key

For server-controlled application code, create a request client using the virtual key:

```go
tenantClient := gateway.NewClient(gatewayURL, key.Key)
result, err := tenantClient.Chat(ctx, "fast", "Summarize the supplied text.")
```

`WithKey` can also copy a client with a different inference key. Keep any client carrying an admin credential inside trusted server code: the copy retains the original admin key for administrative methods.

## Revoke a key

```go
if err := adminClient.RevokeVirtualKey(ctx, key.ID); err != nil {
	return err
}
```

The SDK calls the gateway's revoke endpoint. Subsequent authentication behavior depends on the gateway version and cache propagation; check the response and logs if a key still appears active.

## Read the spend summary

```go
summary, err := adminClient.SpendSummary(ctx)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Printf("Requests: %d; tokens: %d; cost: %d µ$\n",
	summary.TotalRequests, summary.TotalTokens, summary.TotalCostMicros)
fmt.Println("Spend by provider:", summary.SpendByProvider)
```

The summary type currently comes from an internal gateway package, although the SDK method exposes it. The stable JSON API is available at `GET /admin/v1/spend/summary`; see the [cost accounting guide](/docs/finops-and-security/micro-dollar-ledger) and [API reference](/docs/api-reference/gateway-api).

---

## MCP and A2A
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/sdk/mcp-and-a2a
Section: Go SDK Handbook > Go SDK Handbook

# MCP and A2A

The SDK includes public configuration types for registering MCP servers and A2A agents. The gateway exposes the protocol routes for tool calls, agent messages, and tasks. Administrative registration methods require a client authenticated with an admin key and the corresponding server permissions.

## Register and sync an MCP server

```go
serverID, err := gw.AddMCPServer(ctx, gateway.MCPServerConfig{
	Name:      "Example tools",
	Slug:      "example-tools",
	Transport: "streamable_http",
	URL:       "https://tools.example.com/mcp",
	Enabled:   true,
})
if err != nil {
	return err
}

toolCount, err := gw.SyncMCPTools(ctx, serverID)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Printf("Synced %d tools\n", toolCount)
```

The gateway applies outbound network policy to the MCP server URL. Confirm the transport and endpoint path expected by your MCP server before registering it.

## List tools

`ListMCPTools` accepts an empty route for the virtual hub, a server slug, or a `toolsets/{slug}` route:

```go
tools, err := gw.ListMCPTools(ctx, "example-tools")
if err != nil {
	return err
}
for _, tool := range tools {
	fmt.Println(tool["name"], tool["description"])
}
```

The gateway also provides a plain REST bridge for clients that do not use JSON-RPC. See the [MCP overview](/docs/protocols/mcp-overview), [hub and REST bridge](/docs/protocols/mcp-hub-and-rest), and [MCP API reference](/docs/api-reference/mcp-api).

## Register an A2A agent

```go
agentID, err := gw.AddA2AAgent(ctx, gateway.A2AAgentConfig{
	Name:        "Research agent",
	Slug:        "research",
	Description: "Internal research agent",
	EndpointURL: "https://agent.example.com",
})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
fmt.Println("Registered agent:", agentID)
```

Use the [A2A API reference](/docs/api-reference/a2a-api) for message and task request schemas. The SDK's `SendA2AMessage` method currently accepts a protobuf type from an `internal` package, so applications outside the gateway module should use the HTTP API or another supported public client for dispatch.

## Security and permissions

- Use an admin client only for registration and management calls; use scoped virtual keys for application traffic.
- Allow only destinations that should receive gateway requests, and review the outbound SSRF/network policy.
- Disable Stdio MCP servers unless the gateway configuration and deployment are prepared to allow them.

---

## Go SDK API Reference
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/sdk/go-sdk-reference
Section: Go SDK Handbook > Go SDK Handbook

# Go SDK API Reference

Package: `github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway`

The signatures below reflect the public SDK types and methods. A few lower-level helpers expose types from Go's `internal` packages; those are omitted because applications outside the gateway module cannot import those types.

## Constructors and client lifecycle

```go
func New(opts ...Option) (*Client, error)
func NewClient(baseURL, apiKey string) *Client

func (c *Client) WithKey(virtualKey string) *Client
func (c *Client) Close()
func (c *Client) BaseURL() string
```

`New` starts an embedded instance unless configured with `WithRemote`. `NewClient` creates a client for an existing gateway. `Close` shuts down resources created for embedded mode; it is a no-op for a remote client.

## Client options

```go
func WithConfigFile(path string) Option
func WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing() Option
func WithLogLevel(level string) Option
func WithLogger(l *slog.Logger) Option
func WithModelList(entries ...ModelEntry) Option
func WithRemote(baseURL, apiKey string) Option
func WithSilentLogs() Option
```

`Option` is an opaque option type accepted by `New`; its function signature uses an internal configuration type. Applications should pass the built-in options instead of constructing options directly.

## Chat methods

```go
func (c *Client) Chat(ctx context.Context, model, userPrompt string, opts ...RequestOption) (*ChatResult, error)
func (c *Client) ChatWithMessages(ctx context.Context, req ChatRequest, opts ...RequestOption) (*ChatResult, error)
func (c *Client) StreamChat(ctx context.Context, model, userPrompt string, onDelta func(delta string) error, opts ...RequestOption) (*ChatResult, error)
func (c *Client) ListModels(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error)
```

Request options:

```go
func WithSystem(systemPrompt string) RequestOption
func WithTemperature(temp float64) RequestOption
func WithMaxTokens(maxTokens int) RequestOption
func WithReasoningEffort(effort string) RequestOption
```

Pass these helpers to `Chat` or `StreamChat`. The SDK exposes the option type for use with its built-in helpers; applications should not implement custom options because the function signature depends on an internal request type.

## Core data types

```go
type ModelEntry struct {
	ModelName       string
	Model           string
	APIKey          string
	APIBase         string
	RoutingStrategy string
	Fallbacks       []string
	Weight          int
	RPM             int
	TPM             int
	SimulateStatus  int
}

type ChatResult struct {
	Content           string
	ReasoningContent  string
	Provider          string
	Model             string
	RequestID         string
	CostMicros        int64
	RoutingMicros     int64
	CacheStatus       string
	RouteReason       string
	FallbackAttempted bool
    // Usage and Raw are omitted because their concrete types come from internal packages.
}

type ChatRequest struct {
	Model           string
	Messages        []Message
	Temperature     *float64
	TopP            *float64
	MaxTokens       *int
	Stop            []string
	Stream          bool
	ReasoningEffort string
	User            string
}

type Message struct {
	Role       string
	Content    string
	Name       string
	ToolCallID string
	ToolCalls  []ToolCall
}

type ToolCall struct {
	ID       string
	Type     string
	Function FunctionCall
}

type FunctionCall struct {
	Name      string
	Arguments string
}
```

The `ChatResult` excerpt shows the stable top-level fields most applications need. It also has `Usage` and `Raw` fields whose concrete types come from internal packages; prefer top-level fields when you need to avoid depending on those implementation types. JSON tags are omitted here for readability; consult the source for serialization details.

## Virtual keys and protocol registration

```go
func (c *Client) CreateVirtualKey(ctx context.Context, req VirtualKeyRequest) (*VirtualKeyInfo, error)
func (c *Client) RevokeVirtualKey(ctx context.Context, keyID string) error
func (c *Client) AddMCPServer(ctx context.Context, srv MCPServerConfig) (string, error)
func (c *Client) SyncMCPTools(ctx context.Context, serverID string) (int, error)
func (c *Client) ListMCPTools(ctx context.Context, route string) ([]map[string]any, error)
func (c *Client) AddA2AAgent(ctx context.Context, agent A2AAgentConfig) (string, error)
```

The corresponding public configuration types are `VirtualKeyRequest`, `VirtualKeyInfo`, `MCPServerConfig`, and `A2AAgentConfig`. Use the SDK feature guides for examples and required server permissions:

- [Client configuration](./client-configuration)
- [Virtual keys and FinOps](./virtual-keys-and-finops)
- [MCP and A2A](./mcp-and-a2a)

# Go Examples

These small Go programs demonstrate the gateway's SDK, provider integrations, routing, MCP, A2A, and service embedding. Each example lives in its own directory under `examples/`.

---

## 🏃 Running Any Demo

Run an example from the `examples/` module after its Go dependencies are available:

```bash
cd examples
go run ./hello_gateway
```

Most examples enable the built-in mock provider when credentials are missing, so they can demonstrate the request flow without contacting a model provider. Examples that require a local service, such as Ollama or an HTTP server, still need that service running. To test a live provider, export the matching key before running its example:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy... or AQ.Ab8..."
```

The examples module declares its Go toolchain version in `examples/go.mod`. See each example's source for the provider, local service, or environment variables it needs.

## Hello Gateway
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/hello-gateway
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Fundamentals

# Hello Gateway

In this guide, you will initialize the GoRoute AI Gateway in-process with a single model and execute a synchronous chat completion.

---

## Architecture Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller as Go Application
    participant GW as GoRoute AI Gateway (In-Process)
    participant Provider as Upstream LLM / Mock Engine

    Caller->>GW: 1. gateway.New(WithModelList(...))
    Note over GW: Embedded server boots in < 2ms
    Caller->>GW: 2. gw.Chat(ctx, "gpt-4o-mini", "Hello!")
    GW->>Provider: 3. Forward Canonical Request
    Provider-->>GW: 4. Return Completion
    GW-->>Caller: 5. *gateway.ChatResult (Content, Cost, Latency)
```

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/hello_gateway/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("Hello Gateway (Minimal 20-Line In-Process Engine)")

	// 1. Initialize embedded gateway with one model entry
	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "gpt-4o-mini",
				Model:     "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
				APIKey:    "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(), // Uses an in-process mock when the key is missing
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	// 2. Execute chat completion
	res, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "gpt-4o-mini", "Hello! What are you?")
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Chat request failed", err)
	}

	demoutil.Info("Model", res.Model)
	demoutil.Info("Provider", res.Provider)
	demoutil.Info("Routing Latency (µs)", fmt.Sprintf("%d µs", res.RoutingMicros))
	demoutil.Info("Cost (Micro-Dollars)", fmt.Sprintf("%d micros ($%.6f USD)", res.CostMicros, float64(res.CostMicros)/1e6))
	demoutil.Success("Response", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

---

## Execution Output

```text
================================================================================
          Hello Gateway (Minimal 20-Line In-Process Engine)
================================================================================
  • Model                   : gpt-4.1-mini
  • Provider                : openai
  • Routing Latency (µs)    : 1 µs
  • Cost (Micro-Dollars)    : 37 micros ($0.000037 USD)
  ✓ Response                : OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini handled this request through the unified canonical gateway contract.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

## System Prompts
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/system-prompt
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Fundamentals

# System Prompts & Persona Steering

Learn how to steer the model's persona, tone, and constraints using `gateway.WithSystem(...)`. GoRoute automatically translates this to developer messages for reasoning models (`o1`/`o3`) and top-level parameters for Anthropic Claude.

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/system_prompt/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("System Prompts & Persona Steering")

	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "assistant",
				Model:     "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
				APIKey:    "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	// Steer persona using gateway.WithSystem
	res, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "assistant", "What is Go?",
		gateway.WithSystem("You are an ultra-concise technical educator. Answer in exactly 1 sentence."),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Chat request failed", err)
	}

	demoutil.Info("Model", res.Model)
	demoutil.Info("Tokens Used", fmt.Sprintf("Prompt: %d, Completion: %d", res.Usage.PromptTokens, res.Usage.CompletionTokens))
	demoutil.Success("Steered Output", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

---

## Execution Output

```text
================================================================================
                  System Prompts & Persona Steering
================================================================================
  • Model                   : gpt-4.1-mini
  • Tokens Used             : Prompt: 15, Completion: 19
  ✓ Steered Output          : OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini handled this request through the unified canonical gateway contract.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

## Streaming Tokens
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/streaming-tokens
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Fundamentals

# Zero-Buffer SSE Token Streaming

Learn how to consume real-time Server-Sent Events (SSE) token chunks using GoRoute's `gw.StreamChat` method. The engine translates upstream provider streaming protocols with zero internal buffering overhead.

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/streaming_tokens/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("Zero-Buffer SSE Token Streaming")

	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "stream-chat",
				Model:     "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
				APIKey:    "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	renderer := demoutil.NewStreamRenderer("SSE Token Stream")

	// Call StreamChat with a streaming delta chunk handler callback
	_, err = gw.StreamChat(ctx, "stream-chat", "Count from 1 to 5.", func(delta string) error {
		if delta != "" {
			renderer.Add(delta)
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Streaming failed", err)
	}

	renderer.Finish()
	demoutil.Success("Stream Status", "Completed with zero-buffer SSE translation")
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

---

## Execution Output

```text
================================================================================
                   Zero-Buffer SSE Token Streaming
================================================================================
  • SSE Token Stream        : GoRoute AI Gateway streams SSE tokens with sub-millisecond routing overhead. (Stream finished: 3 chunks)
  ✓ Stream Status           : Completed with zero-buffer SSE translation
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

## Temperature & Limits
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/temperature-and-sampling
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Fundamentals

# Temperature and Minimal Output Caps

Learn how to control model randomness and protect your budget with strict generation limits. Setting `WithTemperature(0.0)` guarantees deterministic outputs, while `WithMaxTokens(5)` prevents runaway output billing.

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/temperature_and_sampling/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("Temperature and Minimal Output Caps")

	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "sampling-chat",
				Model:     "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
				APIKey:    "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	// Strict determinism: Temperature 0.0, MaxTokens capped to 5
	res, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "sampling-chat", "Pick a single letter.",
		gateway.WithTemperature(0.0),
		gateway.WithMaxTokens(5),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Request failed", err)
	}

	demoutil.Info("Temperature", "0.0 (Deterministic)")
	demoutil.Info("Max Tokens Cap", "5")
	demoutil.Info("Tokens Consumed", fmt.Sprintf("%d", res.Usage.CompletionTokens))
	demoutil.Success("Deterministic Output", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

## Structured JSON
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/json-mode-structured-output
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Fundamentals

# Guaranteed JSON Mode Structured Outputs

In this guide, you will configure system extraction schemas to guarantee that the model outputs strictly valid, machine-parsable JSON payloads.

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/json_mode_structured_output/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

type WeatherOutput struct {
	City        string  `json:"city"`
	Temperature float64 `json:"temperature_c"`
	Condition   string  `json:"condition"`
}

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("Guaranteed JSON Mode Structured Outputs")

	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "json-chat",
				Model:     "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
				APIKey:    "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	// Enforce valid JSON object output via system instructions
	res, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "json-chat", "Extract: Paris is currently 19.5C and sunny.",
		gateway.WithSystem("You are a structured data extractor. You MUST respond with ONLY a valid JSON object matching: {\"city\": string, \"temperature_c\": number, \"condition\": string}."),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Request failed", err)
	}

	var parsed WeatherOutput
	_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(res.Content), &parsed)

	demoutil.Info("Schema Validation", "JSON Object Validated")
	demoutil.Success("Structured Output", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

## Multi-Turn Memory
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/multi-turn-conversation
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Fundamentals

# Multi-Turn Conversational Memory & Context

Learn how to preserve chat history across multiple turns using `gateway.ChatRequest` with alternating `system`, `user`, and `assistant` messages.

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/multi_turn_conversation/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("Multi-Turn Conversational Memory & Context")

	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "chat",
				Model:     "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
				APIKey:    "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	// Multi-turn context preservation
	req := gateway.ChatRequest{
		Model: "chat",
		Messages: []gateway.Message{
			{Role: "system", Content: "You are a friendly assistant."},
			{Role: "user", Content: "Hi, my favorite programming language is Go."},
			{Role: "assistant", Content: "Hello! That's wonderful to hear. Go is great for scalable concurrency."},
			{Role: "user", Content: "What did I say my favorite language was?"},
		},
	}

	res, err := gw.ChatWithMessages(ctx, req)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Request failed", err)
	}

	demoutil.Info("Turns Processed", "4 messages (System, User, Assistant, User)")
	demoutil.Info("Prompt Tokens", fmt.Sprintf("%d", res.Usage.PromptTokens))
	demoutil.Success("Multi-Turn Memory Response", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

---

## OpenAI Direct
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/openai-direct
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Multi-Provider

# OpenAI Direct Provider Integration

Learn how to connect directly to OpenAI endpoints using the verified low-cost `openai/gpt-4o-mini` tier (\$0.15/1M input tokens).

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/openai_direct/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("OpenAI Direct Provider Integration (Live Test Capable)")

	hasKey := os.Getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") != ""
	if hasKey {
		demoutil.Info("Environment", "Using live OPENAI_API_KEY")
	} else {
		demoutil.Info("Environment", "No OPENAI_API_KEY found; running with zero-config mock")
	}

	// Uses verified lowest-cost model: openai/gpt-4o-mini ($0.15/1M input)
	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "openai-mini",
				Model:     "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
				APIKey:    "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	// Execute with minimal token cap (max 2 tokens) for sub-cent live testing
	res, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "openai-mini", "ping",
		gateway.WithMaxTokens(2),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("OpenAI request failed", err)
	}

	demoutil.Info("Provider", res.Provider)
	demoutil.Info("Model", res.Model)
	demoutil.Info("Cost (Micro-Dollars)", fmt.Sprintf("%d micros ($%.6f USD)", res.CostMicros, float64(res.CostMicros)/1e6))
	demoutil.Success("Response", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

## Local Ollama
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/local-ollama
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Multi-Provider

# Local Offline LLM with Ollama Integration

Learn how to connect GoRoute AI Gateway to local on-premises models running in Ollama (`ollama/llama3.2`) with custom `api_base` URLs.

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/local_ollama/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"
	"strings"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("Local Offline LLM with Ollama Integration")

	// Connect to local Ollama server running on default port 11434
	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "local-llama",
				Model:     "ollama/llama3.2",
				APIBase:   "http://localhost:11434",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	demoutil.Info("Provider", "Ollama (Local / On-Premises)")
	demoutil.Info("Model", "ollama/llama3.2")
	demoutil.Info("Endpoint", "http://localhost:11434")

	res, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "local-llama", "Hello from local inference!",
		gateway.WithMaxTokens(16),
	)
	if err != nil {
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), "connection refused") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "502") {
			demoutil.Info("Daemon Status", "No active Ollama daemon on :11434 (start with 'ollama serve')")
			demoutil.Success("Gateway Verification", "Local endpoint configured cleanly; ready when Ollama daemon starts")
			demoutil.Done()
			return
		}
		demoutil.Fail("Ollama request failed", err)
	}

	demoutil.Info("Cost", "$0.00 (Self-hosted on-premises)")
	demoutil.Success("Local Response", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```

## Unified Model Aliases
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/demos/unified-model-alias
Section: Runnable Go Examples > Multi-Provider

# Decoupling Applications with Unified Model Aliases

In this guide, you will configure a logical model alias (`"production-primary"`). Calling applications request this alias without needing to know which upstream vendor is currently fulfilling the inference.

---

## Runnable Go Code

```go title="examples/unified_model_alias/main.go"
package main

import (
	"context"

	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go-docs/examples/demoutil"
	"github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/pkg/gateway"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	demoutil.Banner("Decoupling Applications with Unified Model Aliases")

	// Clients call "production-primary" without knowing if it's OpenAI, Gemini, or Claude
	gw, err := gateway.New(
		gateway.WithModelList(
			gateway.ModelEntry{
				ModelName: "production-primary",
				Model:     "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite", // Can be swapped to any provider with 0 client changes
				APIKey:    "os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY",
			},
		),
		gateway.WithDemoMocksIfEnvMissing(),
		gateway.WithSilentLogs(),
	)
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Gateway initialization failed", err)
	}
	defer gw.Close()

	// Client requests logical alias "production-primary"
	res, err := gw.Chat(ctx, "production-primary", "What is an architectural abstraction layer?")
	if err != nil {
		demoutil.Fail("Request failed", err)
	}

	demoutil.Info("Logical Requested Model", "production-primary")
	demoutil.Info("Actual Upstream Provider", res.Provider)
	demoutil.Info("Actual Upstream Model", res.Model)
	demoutil.Success("Response", res.Content)
	demoutil.Done()
}
```
