## Model Context Protocol (MCP) API Reference
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/api-reference/mcp-api
Section: API Reference > API Reference

# Model Context Protocol (MCP) API Reference

GoRoute AI Gateway implements the official **MCP 2026-07-28** stateless Streamable HTTP specification with backward compatibility for **MCP 2025-11-25**. It functions as an enterprise Virtual Hub aggregating distributed tool servers, validating schemas, enforcing Virtual Key scopes, and eliminating prompt token overhead with progressive discovery.

> [!NOTE]
> All MCP routes authenticate using the standard Bearer header with a tenant-scoped Virtual API Key:
> ```http
> Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e
> ```

---

## MCP Route Topology

| Protocol Method | Route | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST` | `/mcp` | Virtual Hub multi-server aggregator (`tools/list`, `tools/call`) |
| `POST` | `/mcp/{serverSlug}` | Scoped execution targeted at a single upstream MCP server |
| `POST` | `/mcp/toolsets/{toolsetSlug}` | Execution routed through a curated, vetted toolset |
| `GET` | `/mcp/subscriptions/listen` | Client SSE stream for dynamic catalog invalidation events |
| `GET` | `/mcp-rest/tools/list` | Plain REST list of aggregated tools without JSON-RPC framing |
| `POST` | `/mcp-rest/tools/call` | Plain REST tool execution with direct JSON payloads |
| `GET` | `/v1/goroute/mcp/registry` | Progressive discovery feed issuing 256-bit tool handles |

---

## 1. Virtual Hub Multi-Server Aggregator (`POST /mcp`)

Aggregates all registered, active, and tenant-authorized MCP servers into a single unified JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint. Tool names are automatically namespaced (`<server-slug>__<tool-name>`) to prevent collisions.

### Headers Required
```http
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json, text/event-stream
Origin: http://localhost:8080
Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e
```

### Tool Discovery (`tools/list`)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "tools/list",
    "params": {}
  }'
```

#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "tools": [
      {
        "name": "github__create_issue",
        "description": "Create an issue in a GitHub repository",
        "inputSchema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "owner": { "type": "string" },
            "repo": { "type": "string" },
            "title": { "type": "string" },
            "body": { "type": "string" }
          },
          "required": ["owner", "repo", "title"]
        }
      },
      {
        "name": "fin_tools__calculate_dcf",
        "description": "Calculate discounted cash flow with high precision",
        "inputSchema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "discount_rate": { "type": "number" },
            "cash_flows": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "number" } }
          },
          "required": ["discount_rate", "cash_flows"]
        }
      }
    ],
    "_meta": {
      "goroute.ai/server_outcomes": {
        "github": "success",
        "fin-tools": "success"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Tool Execution via Virtual Hub (`tools/call`)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 2,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "github__create_issue",
      "arguments": {
        "owner": "goroute-ai",
        "repo": "ai-gateway-go",
        "title": "Bug: fix connection pooling",
        "body": "Detailed description of the issue."
      }
    }
  }'
```

#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Issue #42 created successfully at https://github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/issues/42"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false
  }
}
```

---

## 2. Scoped Server Execution (`POST /mcp/{serverSlug}`)

Routes JSON-RPC 2.0 requests exclusively to the upstream server matching `{serverSlug}`. Tool names do not require namespace prefixes in scoped mode.

GoRoute preserves arbitrary decimal precision for financial and scientific tools using Go's `big.Rat` and `json.Number` without IEEE-754 floating point distortion.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp/fin-tools \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 10,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "calculate_dcf",
      "arguments": {
        "discount_rate": 0.08251294819284719,
        "cash_flows": [1000000, 1500000, 2000000]
      }
    }
  }'
```

#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 10,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Net Present Value: 3824192.48291048192"
      }
    ],
    "isError": false
  }
}
```

---

## 3. Curated Toolset Execution (`POST /mcp/toolsets/{toolsetSlug}`)

Executes tool calls through a predefined, vetted subset of pinned tools spanning multiple backend servers. Useful for creating role-restricted environments (e.g. `read-only-analyst`, `devops-tier-1`).

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp/toolsets/analyst-tools \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 20,
    "method": "tools/list",
    "params": {}
  }'
```

---

## 4. Plain MCP REST Bridge (`/mcp-rest/*`)

Standard RESTful endpoints designed for traditional HTTP clients, SDKs, and webhooks that interact without JSON-RPC 2.0 framing.

### List Accessible Tools (`GET /mcp-rest/tools/list`)

#### Query Parameters
- `server_slug` *(optional)*: Filter tools registered under a specific upstream server.

```bash
curl "http://localhost:8080/mcp-rest/tools/list?server_slug=fin-tools" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e"
```

#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "id": "tool_019248ab-3c4d-5e6f",
      "server_id": "mcp_srv_771829a",
      "server_slug": "fin-tools",
      "name": "calculate_dcf",
      "description": "Calculate discounted cash flow with high precision",
      "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "discount_rate": { "type": "number" },
          "cash_flows": { "type": "array" }
        },
        "required": ["discount_rate", "cash_flows"]
      },
      "cost_per_call_micros": 500,
      "is_active": true
    }
  ]
}
```

### Execute Tool Call (`POST /mcp-rest/tools/call`)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp-rest/tools/call \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "server_slug": "fin-tools",
    "tool_name": "calculate_dcf",
    "arguments": {
      "discount_rate": 0.08,
      "cash_flows": [500000, 750000, 1000000]
    }
  }'
```

#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Net Present Value: 1851240.22"
    }
  ],
  "is_error": false
}
```

#### Error Handling
- `HTTP 400 AmbiguousToolName`: Returned when `tool_name` matches multiple active servers and `server_slug` was omitted. Contains a `matching_servers` array.
- `HTTP 403 mcp_server_forbidden`: Caller's Virtual API Key is not authorized for the requested server or toolset.

---

## 5. Progressive Tool Discovery & Public Registry (`GET /v1/goroute/mcp/registry`)

To prevent token exhaustion when exposing hundreds of tools to LLM agent loops, GoRoute issues compact 256-bit cryptographic tool handles (`tool_hdl_<64 hex chars>`).

### Registry Catalog Feed

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/goroute/mcp/registry \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e"
```

#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "servers": [
    {
      "server_slug": "fin-tools",
      "tools": [
        {
          "name": "calculate_dcf",
          "description": "Calculates discounted cash flow valuation",
          "tool_handle": "tool_hdl_a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Dynamic Schema Hydration Meta-Tools

When progressive discovery is active in an agent loop, models only receive tool handles and descriptions. When a model decides to invoke a tool, it calls built-in meta-tools:

1. **`search_tools`**: Keyword search over registered tool definitions:
   ```json
   { "query": "discounted cash flow", "limit": 5 }
   ```
2. **`get_tool_schema`**: Resolves full JSON Schema by handle:
   ```json
   { "tool_handle": "tool_hdl_a1b2c3d4e5f67890123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0" }
   ```
3. **Execution via Handle**: Directly call `POST /mcp-rest/tools/call` using `tool_name: "tool_hdl_..."`. If an upstream schema mutates, stale handles fail-closed with HTTP 404/410.

---

## Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol API Reference
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/api-reference/a2a-api
Section: API Reference > API Reference

# Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol API Reference

GoRoute AI Gateway implements the Linux Foundation **Agent-to-Agent (A2A v1.0)** protocol specification. It serves as an enterprise gateway for autonomous agent discovery, asynchronous multi-step task delegation, real-time event streaming, and cross-framework agent federation.

> [!NOTE]
> All A2A data plane endpoints require standard Bearer token authentication using a tenant Virtual API Key:
> ```http
> Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e
> ```

---

## A2A Endpoints Summary

| Protocol / Method | Endpoint | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GET` | `/.well-known/agent-card.json` | RFC 8785 JCS canonicalized & RFC 7515 JWS signed Agent Card |
| `POST` | `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}` | Dual-binding message dispatch (JSON-RPC 2.0 & HTTP+JSON) |
| `GET` | `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks` | List tasks managed by the agent |
| `GET` | `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID}` | Inspect state, iteration budget, and outputs for a task |
| `POST` | `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID}:cancel` | Safely abort an in-flight task execution |
| `GET` | `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID}:subscribe` | Subscribe-First SSE stream emitting monotonic `a2a-event`s |
| `gRPC` | `lf.a2a.v1.A2AService` | Native high-performance gRPC service |
| `POST` | `/v1/chat/completions` (`model: "a2a/{slug}"`) | OpenAI-compatible bridge for multi-agent workflows |

---

## 1. Cryptographic Agent Card Discovery (`GET /.well-known/agent-card.json`)

Exposes the gateway's canonical agent identity formatted with **RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)** and signed with **RFC 7515 JWS (`ES256`)**. External agents and registries use this card to verify capabilities, cryptographic public keys, and supported endpoints.

### cURL Request

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent-card.json
```

### Response Schema (`HTTP 200 OK`)

```json
{
  "name": "GoRoute AI Gateway Agent Service",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Enterprise Autonomous Routing, Aggregation & Inference Agent",
  "supportedInterfaces": [
    {
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/analyst",
      "protocolBinding": "HTTP+JSON"
    },
    {
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/analyst",
      "protocolBinding": "JSON-RPC-2.0"
    },
    {
      "url": "grpc://localhost:9090",
      "protocolBinding": "gRPC"
    }
  ],
  "capabilities": {
    "streaming": true,
    "asyncTasks": true,
    "pushNotifications": true
  },
  "signatures": [
    {
      "header": {
        "alg": "ES256",
        "kid": "gw-a2a-signer-v1",
        "typ": "JWT"
      },
      "signature": "MEUCIQDx41..."
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 2. Dual-Binding Agent Message Dispatch (`POST /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}`)

Dispatches messages to upstream agents. GoRoute inspects the request body and transparently handles both **JSON-RPC 2.0** and **HTTP+JSON Protobuf REST** formats.

### Option A: JSON-RPC 2.0 Binding (`tasks/send`)

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": "req-a2a-001",
    "method": "tasks/send",
    "params": {
      "message": {
        "role": "ROLE_USER",
        "parts": [
          { "text": "Perform portfolio Value-at-Risk assessment for Portfolio Q3." }
        ]
      }
    }
  }'
```

#### JSON-RPC 2.0 Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": "req-a2a-001",
  "result": {
    "role": "ROLE_AGENT",
    "parts": [
      { "text": "Portfolio risk assessment completed: VaR (95% confidence) is 1.42%." }
    ],
    "taskId": "task_a2a_5b91a7c0",
    "state": "completed"
  }
}
```

### Option B: HTTP+JSON Protobuf Binding

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "message": {
      "role": "ROLE_USER",
      "parts": [
        { "text": "Calculate VaR 99% for portfolio." }
      ]
    },
    "budget": {
      "max_cost_micros": 5000000,
      "max_iterations": 10
    }
  }'
```

---

## 3. Task Management Endpoints

Inspect, list, and control asynchronous agent execution lifecycles.

### Inspect Task Details (`GET /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID}`)

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst/tasks/task_a2a_5b91a7c0 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e"
```

#### Response (`HTTP 200 OK`)
```json
{
  "id": "task_a2a_5b91a7c0",
  "agent_slug": "risk-analyst",
  "state": "working",
  "created_at": "2026-11-10T12:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-10T12:00:05Z",
  "iterations_executed": 3,
  "max_iterations": 10,
  "cost_incurred_micros": 12500
}
```

### Cancel In-Flight Task (`POST /a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks/{taskID}:cancel`)

Safely terminates background execution and prevents further upstream model spend:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst/tasks/task_a2a_5b91a7c0:cancel \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e"
```

---

## 4. Subscribe-First Real-Time SSE Task Streaming (`GET ...:subscribe`)

Clients connect to stream durable task events (status transitions, intermediate thoughts, artifact publications) in real-time. Emits `a2a-event` Server-Sent Events with strictly monotonic sequence numbers (`seq`).

```bash
curl -N http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1/agents/risk-analyst/tasks/task_a2a_5b91a7c0:subscribe \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
```

### Event Stream Wire Format

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive

event: a2a-event
data: {"seq":1,"taskId":"task_a2a_5b91a7c0","state":"working","timestamp":"2026-11-10T12:00:01Z"}

event: a2a-event
data: {"seq":2,"taskId":"task_a2a_5b91a7c0","state":"working","thought":"Fetching historical volatility for 50 tickers...","timestamp":"2026-11-10T12:00:02Z"}

event: a2a-event
data: {"seq":3,"taskId":"task_a2a_5b91a7c0","state":"completed","output":{"role":"ROLE_AGENT","parts":[{"text":"VaR calculation complete."}]},"timestamp":"2026-11-10T12:00:05Z"}
```

---

## 5. Native A2A gRPC Service (`lf.a2a.v1.A2AService`)

For latency-critical agent-to-agent communication, GoRoute exposes a native gRPC server implementing the official Linux Foundation Protobuf contract.

### Protobuf Service Definition

```protobuf
syntax = "proto3";
package lf.a2a.v1;

service A2AService {
  rpc SendMessage(SendMessageRequest) returns (SendMessageResponse);
  rpc GetTask(GetTaskRequest) returns (Task);
  rpc ListTasks(ListTasksRequest) returns (ListTasksResponse);
  rpc CancelTask(CancelTaskRequest) returns (Task);
  rpc SubscribeToTask(SubscribeToTaskRequest) returns (stream StreamTaskResponse);
}
```

### Go gRPC Client Example

```go
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "google.golang.org/grpc"
    "google.golang.org/grpc/metadata"
    pb "github.com/goroute-ai/ai-gateway-go/internal/a2a/pb"
)

func main() {
    conn, _ := grpc.Dial("localhost:9090", grpc.WithInsecure())
    defer conn.Close()

    client := pb.NewA2AServiceClient(conn)
    md := metadata.Pairs("authorization", "Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e")
    ctx := metadata.NewOutgoingContext(context.Background(), md)

    resp, err := client.SendMessage(ctx, &pb.SendMessageRequest{
        AgentSlug: "risk-analyst",
        Message: &pb.Message{
            Role: pb.MessageRole_ROLE_USER,
            Parts: []*pb.Part{pb.NewTextPart("Run risk audit")},
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("Task ID: %s, Response: %v\n", resp.TaskId, resp.Message)
}
```

---

## 6. A2A-to-OpenAI Compatibility Bridge

Allows standard OpenAI Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs to orchestrate multi-agent workflows without changing client libraries by specifying `model: "a2a/{agent_slug}"`.

### cURL Request via Chat Completions

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-prod-7f9a2b8c4d1e" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "a2a/risk-analyst",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Compute Value-at-Risk for Portfolio 4"}
    ]
  }'
```

#### Multi-Turn Resumption (`TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED`)
When an upstream agent requires clarifying input, GoRoute returns an assistant response with `finish_reason: "stop"` containing the agent's question. Callers resume execution simply by sending the next user turn back to `model: "a2a/{agent_slug}"`; GoRoute automatically reconciles conversational context with the active `taskId`.

---

## 7. Emergency Administrative Kill-Switch

Administrators can instantly disable an agent across all cluster nodes using the control plane API:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/v1/a2a/agents/agent_0192ab/kill-switch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GATEWAY_MASTER_ADMIN_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "killed": true }'
```

When tripped, subsequent invocations immediately fail-closed returning `HTTP 503 agent_killed`.

---

## Next Steps

- Explore the [A2A Architectural Guide](/docs/protocols/a2a-overview).
- Review [Model Context Protocol (MCP) APIs](/docs/api-reference/mcp-api).
- Inspect [Audit Logs & FinOps Ledgers](/docs/api-reference/admin-api).

## Integrations Overview
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/overview
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem

# Integrations Overview

GoRoute AI Gateway exposes drop-in **OpenAI-compatible** (`/v1/*`, `/openai/v1/*`) and **Anthropic-compatible** (`/anthropic/v1/*`, `/v1/messages`) wire endpoints, alongside **MCP** (`/mcp*`) and **A2A** (`/a2a/v1/*`) protocol planes. Any client, IDE, CLI agent, or SDK that accepts a custom base URL and API key can route through GoRoute with zero code rewrites.

---

## Base URLs by Protocol

| Client Ecosystem | Base URL | Supported Endpoints | Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **OpenAI-Compatible** | `http://localhost:8080/v1` | `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/realtime`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/audio/*`, `/v1/images/*`, `/v1/files`, `/v1/batches`, `/v1/rerank`, `/v1/moderations` | [Gateway API](/docs/api-reference/gateway-api) |
| **OpenAI Direct Alias** | `http://localhost:8080/openai/v1` | `/openai/v1/responses`, `/openai/v1/realtime` | [Responses API](/docs/data-plane/responses) |
| **Anthropic-Compatible** | `http://localhost:8080/anthropic` | `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `/anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens` (also mounted at `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) | [Anthropic Messages](/docs/data-plane/messages) |
| **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** | `http://localhost:8080/mcp` | `/mcp`, `/mcp/{serverSlug}`, `/mcp/toolsets/{toolsetSlug}`, `/mcp-rest/tools/*` | [MCP Overview](/docs/protocols/mcp-overview) |
| **Agent-to-Agent (A2A)** | `http://localhost:8080/a2a/v1` | `/.well-known/agent-card.json`, `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/`, `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/tasks*` | [A2A Overview](/docs/protocols/a2a-overview) |

---

## Authentication with Virtual Keys (`sk-gw-...`)

Data-plane routes authenticate callers using **Virtual Keys** prefixed with `sk-gw-` (issued via the Operator UI at `/ui/` or `POST /admin/v1/keys`). See [Virtual Keys](/docs/finops-and-security/virtual-keys) for key creation, RBAC scoping, and budget caps.

GoRoute accepts either standard credential header:

- `Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-...` (OpenAI-compatible clients)
- `x-api-key: sk-gw-...` (Anthropic-compatible clients)

> [!NOTE]
> If a client sends **both** `Authorization: Bearer ...` and `x-api-key: ...` with different values, GoRoute rejects the request with `400 Bad Request` (`ambiguous_gateway_credentials`). Identical values in both headers are accepted.

---

## Integration Guides

### Coding Agents & IDEs
- [**Claude Code**](/docs/integrations/claude-code) — Route Claude Code through `/anthropic` using `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- [**Cursor, Continue & Cline**](/docs/integrations/cursor-and-ides) — Configure IDE extensions against `/v1` with Virtual Keys and unified model aliases.
- [**Codex CLI, Gemini CLI & OpenWebUI**](/docs/integrations/codex-and-cli-agents) — Connect terminal coding agents and self-hosted chat UIs via `/v1`.

### Official Language SDKs & Agent Frameworks
- [**OpenAI SDKs (Python & TypeScript)**](/docs/integrations/openai-sdks) — Chat completions, SSE streaming, embeddings, Responses API, and Realtime WebSockets.
- [**Anthropic SDKs (Python & TypeScript)**](/docs/integrations/anthropic-sdks) — Native `/anthropic/v1/messages` and `/anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens`.
- [**Agent Frameworks**](/docs/integrations/agent-frameworks) — LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, and Google ADK with GoRoute MCP and A2A endpoints.

### Observability & Telemetry
- [**OpenTelemetry & Prometheus**](/docs/integrations/otel-and-prometheus) — OTLP/HTTP span export (`tracing.otlp_endpoint`, `gen_ai.*` attributes, W3C `traceparent`) and Prometheus `/metrics` scraping.

---

## Claude Code
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/claude-code
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem > Coding Agents & IDEs

# Claude Code

[Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/overview) uses the Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages`) and token counting (`/v1/messages/count_tokens`). GoRoute exposes both endpoints under `/anthropic/v1/*`, so setting `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to `<GATEWAY_URL>/anthropic` routes all Claude Code traffic through your gateway with full Virtual Key budgets, RBAC, guardrails, and observability.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

1. A running GoRoute AI Gateway instance (for example, `http://localhost:8080`).
2. At least one Anthropic model (or alias such as `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` or `reasoning`) configured in `model_list` or via `/admin/v1/models`.
3. A Virtual Key (`sk-gw-...`) with permission to access the configured model(s).

---

## 2. Environment Configuration

Export `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and your GoRoute Virtual Key before launching `claude`:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080/anthropic"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="sk-gw-your-virtual-key"
```

Alternatively, if you use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (which Claude Code sends via `x-api-key`), set:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080/anthropic"
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-gw-your-virtual-key"
```

> [!WARNING]
> Do not set **both** `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to different values in the same shell. GoRoute validates both `Authorization: Bearer` and `x-api-key` and returns `400 ambiguous_gateway_credentials` if they conflict.

Launch Claude Code:

```bash
claude
```

---

## 3. Model Mapping & Aliases

If your organization uses GoRoute unified aliases (e.g., `fast`, `reasoning`) or routes Claude Code requests to non-Anthropic backends via GoRoute's Anthropic-to-canonical translator, pass `--model` or set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_MODEL="claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
claude --model reasoning
```

GoRoute's `/anthropic/v1/messages` handler normalizes system blocks, `extended_thinking` budgets, and parallel `tool_result` turns automatically. See [Anthropic Messages Ingress API](/docs/data-plane/messages) for translation details.

---

## 4. Connecting Claude Code to GoRoute MCP

You can also point Claude Code at GoRoute's [MCP Virtual Hub](/docs/protocols/mcp-hub-and-rest) so MCP tool calls inherit your Virtual Key RBAC and sandboxing:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "goroute-hub": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer sk-gw-your-virtual-key"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 5. Verification

Confirm the `/anthropic/v1/messages` route responds with your Virtual Key before starting a session:

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/anthropic/v1/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-api-key: sk-gw-your-virtual-key" \
  -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    "max_tokens": 64,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one word."}]
  }'
```

For repository-level agent workflow patterns (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/`, and `AGENTS.md`), see [Engineering Guide for Coding Agents](/docs/operations/claude-code-and-agents).

---

## Cursor, Continue & Cline
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/cursor-and-ides
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem > Coding Agents & IDEs

# Cursor, Continue & Cline

AI-native editors and IDE extensions connect to GoRoute AI Gateway through its OpenAI-compatible `/v1` data plane (`POST /v1/chat/completions`, `GET /v1/models`). Centralizing IDE traffic through GoRoute gives engineering teams unified model aliases, per-developer Virtual Keys, spend caps, and zero-leakage log scrubbing.

---

## Cursor

Cursor supports custom OpenAI-compatible base URLs in **Settings → Models**:

1. Open **Cursor Settings** (`Cmd+,` / `Ctrl+,`) → **Models**.
2. Expand **OpenAI API Key** and enable **Override OpenAI Base URL**.
3. Set the base URL to your GoRoute `/v1` endpoint:
   ```text
   https://gateway.example.com/v1
   ```
   *(For local development without TLS, use `http://localhost:8080/v1`; note that Cursor's cloud-proxied features require a publicly reachable HTTPS endpoint such as a tunnel or ingress.)*
4. Paste your GoRoute Virtual Key (`sk-gw-...`) into **OpenAI API Key** and click **Verify**.
5. Add the model names or aliases configured in your GoRoute `model_list` (for example `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`, or `reasoning`).

---

## Continue (`config.yaml` / `config.json`)

[Continue](https://docs.continue.dev/) supports GoRoute directly via its `openai` provider with `apiBase`.

```yaml title="~/.continue/config.yaml"
name: GoRoute Workspace
version: 1.0.0
schema: v1
models:
  - name: GoRoute Reasoning
    provider: openai
    model: reasoning
    apiBase: http://localhost:8080/v1
    apiKey: sk-gw-your-virtual-key
  - name: GoRoute Fast Autocomplete
    provider: openai
    model: fast
    apiBase: http://localhost:8080/v1
    apiKey: sk-gw-your-virtual-key
    roles:
      - autocomplete
```

---

## Cline (VS Code / Cursor Extension)

[Cline](https://github.com/cline/cline) supports both OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible providers:

### Option A: OpenAI Compatible (Recommended for Multi-Provider Aliases)

1. Open Cline **Settings** (gear icon).
2. Set **API Provider** to **OpenAI Compatible**.
3. Set **Base URL** to `http://localhost:8080/v1`.
4. Set **API Key** to your Virtual Key (`sk-gw-...`).
5. Set **Model ID** to any model or alias configured in GoRoute (e.g., `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` or `gpt-4o`).

### Option B: Anthropic Native Mode

1. Set **API Provider** to **Anthropic**.
2. Enable **Use custom base URL** and set it to `http://localhost:8080/anthropic`.
3. Set **Anthropic API Key** to your Virtual Key (`sk-gw-...`).

---

## Verifying IDE Connectivity

Confirm your Virtual Key can list models and complete a chat request against `/v1`:

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-your-virtual-key"
```

---

## Codex CLI, Gemini CLI & OpenWebUI
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/codex-and-cli-agents
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem > Coding Agents & IDEs

# Codex CLI, Gemini CLI & OpenWebUI

Terminal coding agents and self-hosted chat frontends can point directly at GoRoute's `/v1` endpoints using standard OpenAI-compatible environment variables and Virtual Keys (`sk-gw-...`).

---

## OpenAI Codex CLI

[Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) uses the OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`) and Chat Completions (`/v1/chat/completions`), both of which GoRoute serves under `/v1` and `/openai/v1`.

### Environment Variables

```bash
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-gw-your-virtual-key"
codex --model gpt-4.1
```

### TOML Configuration (`~/.codex/config.toml`)

```toml title="~/.codex/config.toml"
model = "gpt-4.1"
model_provider = "goroute"

[model_providers.goroute]
name = "GoRoute AI Gateway"
base_url = "http://localhost:8080/v1"
env_key = "GOROUTE_API_KEY"
wire_api = "responses"
```

Then export your Virtual Key and run `codex`:

```bash
export GOROUTE_API_KEY="sk-gw-your-virtual-key"
codex
```

---

## Gemini CLI

When using Gemini models configured in GoRoute (such as `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash`), you can route OpenAI-compatible CLI workflows through `/v1`:

```bash
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-gw-your-virtual-key"
```

If you are calling GoRoute directly from scripts or tools expecting a Gemini model alias, configure the model in `config.yaml`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini-2.5-flash
    model_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
```

GoRoute's Gemini adapter translates `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/embeddings` requests into native Gemini API calls while enforcing Virtual Key budgets and SSRF egress policies.

---

## OpenWebUI

[OpenWebUI](https://docs.openwebui.com/) connects to GoRoute as an OpenAI-compatible backend, automatically discovering available models via `GET /v1/models`.

### Docker Environment Variables

```bash
docker run -d -p 3000:8080 \
  -e OPENAI_API_BASE_URL="http://host.docker.internal:8080/v1" \
  -e OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-gw-your-virtual-key" \
  --name open-webui \
  ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main
```

### Admin Panel Configuration

1. Sign in to OpenWebUI as an administrator and go to **Admin Panel → Settings → Connections**.
2. Under **OpenAI API**, set:
   - **URL**: `http://localhost:8080/v1` (or your cluster service URL, e.g., `http://ai-gateway:8080/v1`)
   - **API Key**: `sk-gw-your-virtual-key`
3. Click **Verify Connection** to load your GoRoute model catalog.

---

## OpenAI SDKs (Python & TypeScript)
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/openai-sdks
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem > SDKs & Agent Frameworks

# OpenAI SDKs (Python & TypeScript)

The official `openai` SDKs for Python and TypeScript work with GoRoute AI Gateway by overriding `base_url` / `baseURL` to `http://localhost:8080/v1` and passing a GoRoute Virtual Key (`sk-gw-...`) as `api_key` / `apiKey`.

---

## 1. Client Initialization

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python (openai)" default>

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1",
    api_key="sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript (openai)">

```typescript
const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "http://localhost:8080/v1",
  apiKey: "sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
});
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 2. Chat Completions (`POST /v1/chat/completions`)

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python" default>

```python
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain circuit breakers in one sentence."},
    ],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript">

```typescript
const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-4o-mini",
  messages: [
    { role: "system", content: "You are a concise assistant." },
    { role: "user", content: "Explain circuit breakers in one sentence." },
  ],
});
console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 3. Streaming (`stream: true`)

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python" default>

```python
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Count from 1 to 5."}],
    stream=True,
)
for chunk in stream:
    delta = chunk.choices[0].delta.content
    if delta:
        print(delta, end="", flush=True)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript">

```typescript
const stream = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gpt-4o-mini",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Count from 1 to 5." }],
  stream: true,
});
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  const delta = chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content;
  if (delta) process.stdout.write(delta);
}
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 4. Embeddings (`POST /v1/embeddings`)

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python" default>

```python
emb = client.embeddings.create(
    model="text-embedding-3-small",
    input="GoRoute AI Gateway",
)
print(len(emb.data[0].embedding))
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript">

```typescript
const emb = await client.embeddings.create({
  model: "text-embedding-3-small",
  input: "GoRoute AI Gateway",
});
console.log(emb.data[0].embedding.length);
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 5. Responses API (`POST /v1/responses` & `/openai/v1/responses`)

GoRoute implements the stateful/agentic Responses API at both `/v1/responses` and `/openai/v1/responses`:

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python" default>

```python
resp = client.responses.create(
    model="gpt-4.1-mini",
    input="Summarize the benefits of micro-dollar accounting.",
)
print(resp.output_text)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript">

```typescript
const resp = await client.responses.create({
  model: "gpt-4.1-mini",
  input: "Summarize the benefits of micro-dollar accounting.",
});
console.log(resp.output_text);
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 6. Realtime WebSocket (`GET /v1/realtime` & `/openai/v1/realtime`)

For bidirectional audio/text streaming over WebSockets, connect to `ws://localhost:8080/v1/realtime?model=gpt-4o-realtime-preview` (or `wss://...` in production) with `Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-your-virtual-key`:

```typescript
const ws = new WebSocket(
  "ws://localhost:8080/v1/realtime?model=gpt-4o-realtime-preview",
  {
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
    },
  }
);

ws.on("open", () => {
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "response.create" }));
});
```

See [Realtime WebSocket API](/docs/data-plane/realtime) and [Gateway API Reference](/docs/api-reference/gateway-api) for the full list of supported OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

## Anthropic SDKs (Python & TypeScript)
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/anthropic-sdks
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem > SDKs & Agent Frameworks

# Anthropic SDKs (Python & TypeScript)

The official Anthropic SDKs (`anthropic` in Python and `@anthropic-ai/sdk` in TypeScript) append `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` to their configured base URL. Pointing `base_url` / `baseURL` to `http://localhost:8080/anthropic` routes requests directly to GoRoute's `/anthropic/v1/messages` and `/anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens` endpoints.

---

## 1. Client Initialization

Pass your GoRoute Virtual Key (`sk-gw-...`) as `api_key` / `apiKey` (sent via `x-api-key`) or `auth_token` / `authToken` (sent via `Authorization: Bearer`).

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python (anthropic)" default>

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="http://localhost:8080/anthropic",
    api_key="sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript (@anthropic-ai/sdk)">

```typescript
const client = new Anthropic({
  baseURL: "http://localhost:8080/anthropic",
  apiKey: "sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
});
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

> [!NOTE]
> Avoid setting both `api_key` (`x-api-key`) and `auth_token` (`Authorization: Bearer`) to different values. GoRoute rejects conflicting credential headers with `400 ambiguous_gateway_credentials`.

---

## 2. Messages (`POST /anthropic/v1/messages`)

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python" default>

```python
message = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    max_tokens=256,
    system="You are a concise systems engineer.",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is a sliding-window rate limiter?"}
    ],
)
print(message.content[0].text)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript">

```typescript
const message = await client.messages.create({
  model: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  max_tokens: 256,
  system: "You are a concise systems engineer.",
  messages: [
    { role: "user", content: "What is a sliding-window rate limiter?" },
  ],
});
console.log(message.content[0]);
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 3. Streaming Messages (`stream: true`)

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python" default>

```python
with client.messages.stream(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    max_tokens=256,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "List three Go concurrency primitives."}],
) as stream:
    for text in stream.text_stream:
        print(text, end="", flush=True)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript">

```typescript
const stream = client.messages.stream({
  model: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  max_tokens: 256,
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "List three Go concurrency primitives." }],
});

stream.on("text", (text) => process.stdout.write(text));
await stream.finalMessage();
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 4. Token Counting (`POST /anthropic/v1/messages/count_tokens`)

GoRoute computes pre-flight token counts locally without forwarding to the upstream provider:

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python" default>

```python
count = client.messages.count_tokens(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Estimate tokens for this prompt."}],
)
print(count.input_tokens)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript">

```typescript
const count = await client.messages.countTokens({
  model: "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
  messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Estimate tokens for this prompt." }],
});
console.log(count.input_tokens);
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

See [Anthropic Messages Ingress API](/docs/data-plane/messages) for details on extended thinking blocks, tool schema translation, and alternating turn consolidation.

---

## Agent Frameworks (LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK & Google ADK)
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/agent-frameworks
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem > SDKs & Agent Frameworks

# Agent Frameworks

Agentic frameworks can route both **LLM inference** (`/v1` or `/anthropic`) and **tool/agent protocols** ([MCP](/docs/protocols/mcp-overview) and [A2A](/docs/protocols/a2a-overview)) through GoRoute AI Gateway.

---

## 1. LangChain (Python & TypeScript)

Point `ChatOpenAI` or `ChatAnthropic` at GoRoute using your Virtual Key (`sk-gw-...`):

<Tabs>
  <TabItem value="python" label="Python (langchain-openai)" default>

```python
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(
    model="reasoning",
    base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1",
    api_key="sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
)

resp = llm.invoke("Design a fallback chain for 503 outages.")
print(resp.content)
```

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem value="typescript" label="TypeScript (@langchain/openai)">

```typescript
const llm = new ChatOpenAI({
  model: "reasoning",
  apiKey: "sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
  configuration: {
    baseURL: "http://localhost:8080/v1",
  },
});

const resp = await llm.invoke("Design a fallback chain for 503 outages.");
console.log(resp.content);
```

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 2. OpenAI Agents SDK

The [OpenAI Agents SDK](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/) works with GoRoute by passing a custom `AsyncOpenAI` client configured with `base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1"` and your Virtual Key:

```python
from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from agents import Agent, Runner, set_default_openai_client

client = AsyncOpenAI(
    base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1",
    api_key="sk-gw-your-virtual-key",
)
set_default_openai_client(client)

agent = Agent(
    name="TriageAgent",
    model="gpt-4.1-mini",
    instructions="Route infrastructure questions concisely.",
)

result = await Runner.run(agent, "How does GoRoute enforce SSRF protection?")
print(result.final_output)
```

---

## 3. Google ADK (Agent Development Kit)

In Google ADK, you can either route model calls through GoRoute's OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint or expose/consume remote agents over GoRoute's **A2A v1.0** plane:

1. **Model Routing via `/v1`**:
   Set `OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://localhost:8080/v1"` and `OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-gw-your-virtual-key"` for OpenAI-compatible model wrappers, with Gemini models declared in GoRoute's `model_list` (e.g., `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash`).
2. **A2A Agent Discovery & Dispatch**:
   GoRoute serves A2A agent cards at `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` and task endpoints under `/a2a/v1/agents/{agentSlug}/` (`POST /`, `GET /tasks`, `GET /tasks/{taskID}`, `POST /tasks/{taskID}:cancel`, `GET|POST /tasks/{taskID}:subscribe`). See [A2A Agent Cards](/docs/protocols/a2a-agent-cards).

---

## 4. Connecting Frameworks to GoRoute MCP

Any framework supporting **Streamable HTTP MCP** or **REST tool calls** can consume tools governed by GoRoute's MCP Virtual Hub:

| Protocol | Endpoint | Auth Header | Guide |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MCP Virtual Hub (All Allowed Tools)** | `POST http://localhost:8080/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-...` | [MCP Hub & REST](/docs/protocols/mcp-hub-and-rest) |
| **Scoped MCP Server** | `POST http://localhost:8080/mcp/{serverSlug}` | `Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-...` | [MCP Overview](/docs/protocols/mcp-overview) |
| **Curated MCP Toolset** | `POST http://localhost:8080/mcp/toolsets/{toolsetSlug}` | `Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-...` | [Progressive Discovery](/docs/protocols/mcp-progressive-discovery) |
| **MCP REST Bridge** | `GET /mcp-rest/tools/list`, `POST /mcp-rest/tools/call` | `Authorization: Bearer sk-gw-...` | [MCP Hub & REST](/docs/protocols/mcp-hub-and-rest) |

---

## OpenTelemetry & Prometheus
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/integrations/otel-and-prometheus
Section: Integrations & Ecosystem > Observability & Telemetry

# OpenTelemetry & Prometheus

GoRoute AI Gateway provides built-in **OTLP/HTTP distributed tracing** (`internal/observability/tracing_otlp.go`) and **Prometheus 0.0.4 metrics** (`GET /metrics`). All outbound OTLP exports pass through GoRoute's outbound SSRF `network.Policy`.

---

## 1. OpenTelemetry (OTLP/HTTP) Configuration

Configure `tracing` in `config.yaml`:

```yaml title="config.yaml"
tracing:
  otlp_endpoint: "https://otel-collector.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4318/v1/traces"
  service_name: "ai-gateway-go"
  headers:
    Authorization: "Bearer ${OTEL_EXPORTER_TOKEN}"
```

### Configuration Fields

| Field | Default | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `tracing.otlp_endpoint` | `""` (disabled / no-op tracer) | OTLP/HTTP collector URL. If the path is empty or `/`, GoRoute automatically appends `/v1/traces`. Validated against the outbound `network.Policy` at startup. |
| `tracing.service_name` | `"ai-gateway-go"` | Sets the OpenTelemetry `service.name` resource attribute. |
| `tracing.headers` | `{}` | Optional key-value headers attached to OTLP/HTTP export requests (e.g., `Authorization`, `x-scope-orgid`). |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Because `tracing.otlp_endpoint` is validated by `internal/security/network`, loopback or private collector addresses (such as `http://localhost:4318` or cluster-internal services) require the collector host/CIDR to be permitted in your `network` security policy if private-IP blocking is enabled.

---

## 2. W3C `traceparent` & `gen_ai.*` Span Attributes

GoRoute's `TraceMiddleware` extracts incoming W3C `traceparent` (or `X-Trace-Id`) headers, generates a 128-bit TraceID + 64-bit SpanID when absent, echoes `traceparent` and `X-Trace-Id` on responses, and propagates `traceparent` to upstream providers.

Upstream inference spans are emitted as `gen_ai.client` with OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions:

| Attribute | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `gen_ai.operation.name` | Operation name (e.g., `chat`, `embeddings`). |
| `gen_ai.system` | Upstream provider identifier (e.g., `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`). |
| `gen_ai.request.model` | Target model name dispatched to the provider. |
| `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` | Prompt / input token count. |
| `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` | Completion / output token count. |
| `gen_ai.usage.total_tokens` | Total tokens consumed. |

---

## 3. OTel Collector, Jaeger & Grafana Tempo

Point `tracing.otlp_endpoint` to your OpenTelemetry Collector HTTP receiver (port `4318`), then fan out to Jaeger or Grafana Tempo:

```yaml title="otel-collector-config.yaml"
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [otlp/tempo]
```

- **Jaeger (v1.35+ native OTLP)**: Point `tracing.otlp_endpoint` directly to `http://<jaeger-host>:4318/v1/traces`.
- **Grafana Tempo**: Point `tracing.otlp_endpoint` to `http://<tempo-host>:4318/v1/traces` (or route via OTel Collector above).

---

## 4. Prometheus Scraping (`GET /metrics`)

GoRoute exposes Prometheus text exposition format `0.0.4` at `GET /metrics`. The endpoint is protected by `metricsAuthMiddleware` and requires the **Master Admin Key** in `Authorization: Bearer <MASTER_ADMIN_KEY>` or `x-api-key: <MASTER_ADMIN_KEY>`.

```yaml title="deployments/prometheus/prometheus.yml"
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
  evaluation_interval: 15s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: "ai-gateway-cluster"
    authorization:
      type: Bearer
      credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/secrets/master_admin_key
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["ai-gateway-1:8080", "ai-gateway-2:8080"]
        labels:
          cluster: "prod-verification"
```

For the full catalog of exported `gateway_*` metrics, health probes (`/healthz`, `/readyz`), and structured log scrubbing, see [Observability, Metrics & Health Probes](/docs/operations/observability).

---

## Release Notes
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/release-notes
Section: Release Notes > Release Notes

# Release Notes

GoRoute AI Gateway follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html) and [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/). Each release includes automated SQL schema migrations, OpenAPI contract validation, and multi-replica Kubernetes verification.

---

## Release History

| Version | Release Date | Highlights |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **[v1.6.0](./v1.6.0.md)** | 2026-11-13 | Maximum provider & model compatibility, modality FinOps, `0012` migration, hardened Kustomize manifests (`deployments/k8s/`), and containerized production test suite. |
| **[v1.5.0](./v1.5.0.md)** | 2026-11-13 | Operator RBAC & inbound JWT/OIDC, Redis Cluster/Sentinel support, durable spend outbox, shared circuit breakers, streaming guardrail redaction, and OTLP tracing. |

---

## Upgrade Guide

### 1. Review Breaking & Security Changes
Before upgrading across minor versions:
- Check the target release notes for any new required environment variables or production validation rules (for example, `v1.5.0` introduced `GATEWAY_ENV=production` default-secret rejection and disabled master-key data-plane fallback).
- Review `configs/config.example.yaml` for newly added configuration blocks.

### 2. Database Migrations
GoRoute embeds all PostgreSQL migrations (`migrations/0001_*.sql` through `0012_*.sql`) directly in the gateway binary and applies pending up-migrations atomically at startup.

For zero-downtime rolling upgrades in Kubernetes:
1. Ensure your PostgreSQL user has DDL permissions (`CREATE TABLE`, `ALTER TABLE`, `CREATE INDEX`) or run a pre-upgrade migration job.
2. Take a PostgreSQL snapshot before applying major schema changes (such as `0008` spend outbox or `0012` cache-write and operations columns).
3. Upgrade the gateway image tag and monitor `/readyz` before draining old pods:

```bash
kubectl -n goroute-prod set image deployment/gateway gateway=goroute/ai-gateway:v1.6.0
kubectl -n goroute-prod rollout status deployment/gateway --timeout=120s
```

### 3. Verify Post-Upgrade Health
After rollout completes:
- Confirm `GET /healthz` and `GET /readyz` return `200 OK`.
- Run `make test-canary` against a staging environment to validate live provider routing and modality endpoints.

---

## v1.6.0
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/release-notes/v1.6.0
Section: Release Notes > Release Notes

# Release v1.6.0

**Release Date:** 2026-11-13  
**Theme:** Maximum Provider & Model Compatibility, Modality FinOps, Production Test Suite & K8s Hardening

---

## Model Catalog, Provider Compatibility & Operation Enforcement

- **Upstream Catalog Parity & Capability Generalizations** (`cmd/catalog-sync/`, `internal/modelcatalog/`): Expanded `cmd/catalog-sync` and `internal/modelcatalog` with operation-level model support, modality pricing provenance, and explicit inferred capability generalizations (`internal/modelcatalog/generalizations.go`) without treating unverified catalog rates as verified for budgeted traffic.
- **Operation-Level Routing Enforcement & Certified OpenAI-Compatible Profiles** (`internal/router/`, `internal/adapter/openaicompat/`): Added `SupportedOperations` enforcement across router dispatch (`internal/router/reliability.go`) and expanded certified provider profiles (`internal/adapter/openaicompat/extended_profiles.go`, `validator.go`).
- **Multimodal Native Adapter & Responses API Extensions** (`internal/adapter/`): Expanded multimodal content, tool-only streaming, and audio/image/rerank wire handling across native adapters (`anthropic`, `bedrock`, `cohere`, `gemini`, `mistral`, `ollama`, `openai`, `vertex`) and `/v1/responses`.

---

## Storage, FinOps & Security Fixes

- **Migration `0012` & Modality Persistence** (`migrations/`): Added `migrations/0012_add_cache_write_and_operations.{up,down}.sql` for cache-write pricing and per-model operation declarations across PostgreSQL and in-memory repositories.
- **PostgreSQL `file_uploads` Query Fix** (`internal/storage/postgres.go`): Removed invalid `::uuid` casts on `VARCHAR(64)` `org_id`, `team_id`, and `user_id` columns in `CreateFile`, `GetFile`, `ListFiles`, and `DeleteFile`.
- **In-Memory Spend Outbox & Redis Breaker Fixes** (`internal/storage/`, `internal/cache/`): Deleted delivered entries from `MemoryRepository.spendOutbox` in `MarkSpendEventDelivered` to prevent $O(N^2)$ lock scans under sustained soak load, and treated `redis.Nil` cache misses as non-failures in `RedisFabric` circuit breakers.

---

## Production Testing, Docker & Kubernetes Hardening

- **Hardened Kubernetes Kustomize Manifests** (`deployments/k8s/`): Added `deployments/k8s/` with a 2-replica `gateway` deployment, non-root `securityContext` (`runAsNonRoot: true`, `runAsUser: 65532`, `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`), `/readyz` + `/healthz` probes, and `postgres` + `redis` services. See [Kubernetes & Kustomize Deployment](../operations/kubernetes-kustomize.md).
- **Containerized Production Suite & Load/Canary Harnesses** (`deployments/`, `tests/`): Added `deployments/docker-compose.test.yml`, `tests/load/` (5-minute Go soak + `k6_gateway_smoke.js`), `tests/canary/` (`//go:build canary`), `tests/e2e/budget_concurrency_test.go`, `tests/e2e/modality_compat_test.go`, `tests/e2e/security_boundaries_test.go`, and `make test-prod-containers` (`gitleaks`, `trivy`, `govulncheck`, `k6`, `pgbench`, `redis-benchmark`).

---

## v1.5.0
URL: https://goroute-ai.github.io/docs/release-notes/v1.5.0
Section: Release Notes > Release Notes

# Release v1.5.0

**Release Date:** 2026-11-13  
**Theme:** Enterprise Security Hardening, Redis Cluster Support, Durable FinOps, Streaming Guardrails & API Parity

---

## Security & Multi-Tenant Authorization

- **Operator RBAC & Inbound JWT/OIDC** (`internal/auth/`, `internal/server/handlers_admin.go`): Added role-based operator authorization (`platform_admin`, `org_admin`, `org_viewer`) with organization-scoped control-plane enforcement, inbound JWT/OIDC verification, and disabled master-key data-plane fallback.
- **Fail-Closed Team Lookup & Allowlist Persistence** (`internal/storage/postgres.go`): Enforced fail-closed team lookup error handling and persisted all team allowlists (`allowed_models`, `allowed_mcp_servers`, `allowed_a2a_agents`, `allowed_client_apps`) in PostgreSQL.
- **HTTP Security Headers & CORS Middleware** (`internal/server/security_headers.go`): Added `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` (HSTS opt-in via `server.enable_hsts`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Content-Security-Policy`) and safe-by-default `CORSMiddleware` (`server.cors_allowed_origins`, `server.cors_allow_credentials`).
- **Per-Organization File Storage Quota & Upload Concurrency Limits** (`internal/server/handlers_files.go`): Added `server.max_file_storage_bytes_per_org` (default `5 GiB`, `GATEWAY_MAX_FILE_STORAGE_BYTES_PER_ORG`) and `server.max_concurrent_file_uploads` (default `8`, `GATEWAY_MAX_CONCURRENT_FILE_UPLOADS`) with atomic in-flight reservation tracking (`413 storage_quota_exceeded`), bounded upload semaphore (`429 upload_concurrency_limit`), and explicit `MultipartForm.RemoveAll()` temporary spill-file cleanup.
- **Production Environment Hardening** (`internal/config/config.go`): Updated `Config.Validate()` to treat both `ENV=production` and `GATEWAY_ENV=production` as production signals and reject default admin, encryption, or JWT secrets.
- **Credential & Key Hygiene**: Restricted query-string credentials strictly to WebSocket upgrades (`/v1/realtime`), enforced expiry and revocation on cached virtual keys, and updated `golang.org/x/net` to `v0.62.0`.
- **CI & Supply-Chain Security**: Pinned all GitHub Actions workflows (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`) to immutable 40-character commit SHAs, added `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` for Go and JavaScript/TypeScript analysis, and added `.gitleaks.toml`.

---

## FinOps & Durable Micro-Dollar Accounting

- **Durable Spend Event Outbox** (`migrations/0008_add_spend_event_outbox.up.sql`): Added PostgreSQL spend event outbox with retryable delivery and idempotent Redis spend reconciliation keyed by event ID (`gw:spend:applied:{org}`).
- **Upper-Bound Budget Reservations & Lease Renewal** (`internal/finops/`, `internal/ratelimit/`): Added pre-dispatch upper-bound budget reservation with automatic lease renewal for long-running/streaming requests and unified modality budget gating.
- **Budget Reset Period Advancement & PG/Redis Sync** (`migrations/0011_budget_reset_outbox.up.sql`): Fixed `PostgresRepository.ResetExpiredBudgetsWithIDs`, synchronized entity `spent_micros`, and cleared Redis spend counters on period rollover.
- **Unpriced Usage & Modality Estimates**: Surfaced `unpriced_requests` and `unpriced_tokens` in spend summaries instead of silently recording zero cost, and improved preflight token estimates for modality requests.

---

## Routing, Reliability & Redis Cluster

- **Redis Cluster & Sentinel Support** (`internal/storage/`, `internal/cache/`): Upgraded `RedisFabric` to `go-redis` `UniversalClient` (`storage.redis_addrs`, `storage.redis_master_name`) with `{org:<id>}` hash-tagged Lua keys across rate limiting and response caching.
- **Embeddings Reliability & Shared Circuit Breakers** (`internal/router/`): Wired `ExecuteEmbeddings` through `ReliabilityManager` retries/fallbacks, shared circuit-breaker failure counts and half-open probe leases in Redis across replicas, and fixed adaptive routing signals and least-busy reservation tracking.
- **Bounded Fallback Traversal & Streaming Retries**: Added cycle and depth limits to fallback group traversal and exponential backoff for streaming retries before first output token.

---

## Guardrails, MCP & A2A

- **All-Role Scanning, Streaming Redaction & `logging_only` Mode** (`internal/guardrails/stream_filter.go`, `migrations/0010_guardrail_mode.up.sql`): Expanded input scanning to all message roles, added output blocking and streaming chunk inspection/redaction, and added `logging_only` guardrail policy mode.
- **Fail-Closed Policy & Full Inference Coverage**: Enforced fail-closed guardrail policy lookups, added provider-neutral scanner hooks, and extended guardrail evaluation across all supported inference endpoints.
- **A2A & MCP Hardening** (`internal/a2a/`, `internal/mcp/`): Closed the A2A OpenAI bridge bypass, wired inbound/outbound A2A guardrails (`RouterService.SetGuardrails`), hardened MCP guardrail evaluation, and wired the native A2A gRPC server behind `server.grpc_port` (`GATEWAY_GRPC_PORT`).

---

## API Compatibility & Distributed Caching

- **OpenAI & Anthropic Wire Fidelity** (`internal/adapter/`): Added forwarding for `extra_body` and unknown top-level parameters (`ExtraParams`), Anthropic-formatted error envelopes on `/v1/messages`, streaming TTS (`/v1/audio/speech`), and `tools` forwarding on `/v1/responses`.
- **Canonical Response Cache Keys & Shared Invalidation** (`internal/cache/`): Keyed response cache entries by full canonical output-affecting request fields and propagated cache invalidation epochs across replicas via Redis.

---

## Observability & Embedded Operator Web UI

- **OTLP Distributed Tracing & Uniform Reservoir Sampling** (`internal/observability/`): Added optional OTLP/HTTP distributed tracing (`tracing.otlp_endpoint`, `gen_ai.*` span attributes) routed through the outbound SSRF policy, and replaced rolling-overwrite latency histograms with Vitter Algorithm R uniform reservoir sampling.
- **Structured Log Scrubbing & Protected Metrics** (`internal/logger/`): Added `logger.ScrubSecrets` to mask credentials in structured logs, protected `/metrics` with admin bearer authentication, and bounded Prometheus label cardinality.
- **Operator Web UI Hardening** (`web/`, `internal/ui/`): Repaired JSON field bindings, cleared React Query cache on Control Plane lock, self-hosted fonts (zero external font CDN calls), decoupled Playground/Agentic secrets, added `GET /admin/v1/mcp/tools`, and enforced CI `internal/ui/dist` parity.
